1-1 
1. Introduction 
This document provides information about the BUYPASS® platform (BUYPASS) ATL105 
message formats (software version ATL105).  This format is generally used when a BUYPASS 
customer device accesses BUYPASS directly. 
The scope of the information contained in this document is described in the chapter descriptions 
listed below. 
The audiences of this document include decision makers evaluating BUYPASS services and the 
programmers and analysts who implement and support these services. 
Note: It is important to note that sending of Payment Application Data Security Standard (PA-
DSS) sensitive information, for example PAN, in any field, other than those designated to 
contain such information, is strictly prohibited and can lead to adverse consequences. 
This document contains the following chapters and appendices: 
1.  Introduction.  This chapter lists and describes each chapter in this document. 
2.  Message Flow Overview.  This chapter describes the flow of messages from a BUYPASS 
customer device to BUYPASS. 
3.  Specifications Requirements.  This chapter provides information about the hardware and 
software requirements necessary to support these specifications. 
4.  Supported Industries. This chapter provides information about the industries supported by 
these specifications. 
5.  Supported Payment Network Types. This chapter provides information about the payment 
network types supported by these specifications. 
6.  PIN Encryption Processing.  This chapter provides diagrams and textual information about 
PIN encryption key management relative to using these specifications. 
7.  Network Management Processing.  This chapter provides information about messages 
involved in the network management process relative to using these specifications. 
8.  Store-and-Forward Processing.  This chapter discusses store-and-forward processing for 
automated fuel pumps and the restaurant and lodging industry. 
9.  End-of-Day Processing.  This chapter provides sample information about end-of-day 
processing using a customer-designed electronic journal feature. 
10.  Processing Requirements.  This chapter provides information about credit card, debit 
card, electronic benefits transfer card, fleet card, stored value card, check, loyalty, software 
update, electronic mail, TransArmor, Payment Tokenization, and EMV processing requirements. 
11.  Message Formats.  This chapter provides information about message formats. 
12.  Data Segment Formats.  This chapter provides information about data segment formats. 
13.  Data Element Descriptions.  This chapter provides detailed information about the data 
elements used in the messages described in chapter 11, “Message Formats.” 
14.  Support, Testing, and Certification.  This chapter provides information about 
development support provided to customers by BUYPASS before, during, and after project 
development. 
Appendix A.  TCP/IP Message Header.  This appendix contains TCP/IP message header 
information. 
Appendix B.  POS Purchase Example.  This appendix provides an example of the data layout 
for a POS purchase.

2.3 Unsuccessful Financial Transactions 
This section contains the following examples of unsuccessful financial transactions: 
• Time-out by customer's host/controller/POS system 
• Time-out by customer’s host/device system (late approved response) 
• BUYPASS response not recognized by customer's host/controller/POS system 
A time-out reversal (TOR) is created for an unsuccessful financial transaction.  A TOR never 
initiates a new financial transaction request. 
Notes: A TOR is generated when any of the following transactions is unsuccessful: 
• POS Purchase/Capture transaction 
• CAT Purchase/Capture transaction 
• Mail/Phone Purchase transaction 
A TOR is not supported for either of the following transactions: 
• Debit POS Capture transaction 
• Debit CAT Capture transaction

2-5 
2.3.1 Time-out by Customer's Host/Controller/POS System 
This section describes the transaction flow for an unsuccessful financial transaction (request 
and response) resulting from a time-out by a customer’s host/controller/POS system. 
This transaction flow describes single threading (one transaction at a time); however, any 
combination of requests and responses can be in process at any given time. 
A time-out occurs at the customer’s host/controller/POS system when either of the following 
situations occurs: 
• The customer’s 30-second response interval expires without a response from BUYPASS. 
• A response from BUYPASS is received after the customer’s 30-second response interval 
expires. 
If the customer’s host/controller/POS system receives a late response to the original transaction 
request from BUYPASS, the late response is ignored.  In the event the customer’s 
host/controller/POS system receives more than three consecutive time-outs in an IP 
environment, the line to BUYPASS is marked “down,” and a communications test/health 
message is sent every 30 seconds until a valid response is received from BUYPASS. 
Once a time-out occurs for a device, the customer’s host/controller/POS system formats a TOR, 
which is queued in the customer’s host/controller/POS system until the next financial transaction 
is initiated for that device.  A TOR must be sent from the same device as the original financial 
transaction request that resulted in the TOR.  When the next financial transaction is initiated 
from that device, the queued TOR is transmitted to BUYPASS ahead of the new financial 
transaction request.  If a new financial transaction is not submitted between the occurrence of 
the TOR and the end-of-day settlement, the TOR should be sent to the host immediately prior to 
the settlement request.  Some customer host/controller/POS systems allow transactions to be 
approved and processed in an off-line mode.  When the host/controller/POS system detects that 
the line to BUYPASS is back “up,” the off-line transactions are forwarded to BUYPASS only 
after a valid response is received for all queued TOR’s. 
The Sequence Number, Account Number, and dollar amount—assigned by the customer’s 
host/controller/POS system—are the elements used to match a request with its respective 
response.  The Sequence Number of a TOR must be the same as the Sequence Number of the 
financial transaction being reversed.  Each time any financial transaction request is forwarded to 
BUYPASS, the financial transaction should be assigned a new Sequence Number by the 
customer’s host/controller/POS system. 
Any response from BUYPASS to a TOR, whether it is an approval or a decline, is considered a 
valid response and should clear the TOR from the customer’s host/controller/POS queue.  The 
customer’s host/controller/POS system should continue to send the TOR—subject to health 
message rules—to BUYPASS until a valid response is received.  If no valid response is 
received after three attempts on each available connection route, an error should be logged in 
the electronic journal, and the TOR should be cleared from the queue. 
BUYPASS declines a TOR request as an unmatched reversal when BUYPASS has not 
received the original financial transaction request related to the TOR; or when the original 
financial transaction has already been reversed. 
The following message flow illustrates an unsuccessful financial transaction (request and 
response) resulting from a time-out by a customer's host/controller/POS system:

2.3.3 BUYPASS Response Not Recognized by Customer's 
Host/Controller/POS System 
This section discusses an unsuccessful financial transaction (request and response) resulting 
from the BUYPASS response not being recognized by the customer's host/controller/POS. 
This transaction flow describes single threading (one transaction at a time); however, any 
combination of requests and responses can be in process at any given time.  This flow applies 
to financial transactions including TOR’s. 
If a customer’s host/controller/POS system receives a response from BUYPASS that is not 
correctly formatted or for which the CRC value is incorrect, it should recognize this as a system 
error.  Once a system error is detected, the customer’s host/controller/POS system formats a 
TOR, which is queued in the customer’s host/controller/POS system until the next financial 
transaction is initiated for that device.  A TOR must be sent from the same device as the original 
financial transaction request that resulted in the TOR.  When the next financial transaction is 
initiated from that device, the queued TOR is transmitted to BUYPASS ahead of the new 
financial transaction request.  If a new financial transaction is not submitted between the 
occurrence of the TOR and the end-of-day settlement, the TOR should be sent to the host 
immediately prior to the settlement request. 
The Sequence Number, Account Number, and dollar amount—assigned by the customer's 
host/controller/POS system—are the elements used to match a request with its respective 
response.  The Sequence Number of a TOR must be the same as the Sequence Number of the 
financial transaction being reversed.  Each time any financial transaction request is forwarded to 
BUYPASS, the financial transaction should be assigned a new Sequence Number by the 
customer’s host/controller/POS system. 
Any response from BUYPASS to a TOR, whether it is an approval or a decline, is considered a 
valid response and should clear the TOR from the queue. 
BUYPASS declines a TOR request as an unmatched reversal when BUYPASS has not 
received the original financial transaction request related to the TOR; or when the original 
financial transaction has already been reversed. 
The following information illustrates an unsuccessful financial transaction (request and 
response) resulting from a time-out by a customer's host/controller/POS system:

2.3.4 Summary of TOR Processing Rules 
 
Refer to the below list for a summary of TOR processing rules that are described in detail in the 
above sections: 
 
• A TOR should never be attempted more than 3 times.   
• A TOR is considered complete with any response from the host, except a timeout or no 
response from the host. An approval and decline response are both considered to be a 
successful termination of the TOR and the TOR should be removed from the transaction 
queue.  
• A TOR can only be sent for financial transactions. To remove the hold on an authorization 
only transaction, the device must send a cancellation transaction instead of a TOR.   
• A TOR is not supported for a debit completion.  
• Multiple transactions, and multiple TORs, can be in-flight at any given time. The terminal or 
device is responsible for tracking the status and maintaining the queue of the outstanding 
transactions.   
• When attempting to submit a TOR for a completion transaction, the device must finalize the 
TOR processing prior to resubmitting the completion. If the completion is resent before the 
TOR processing has been completed, the device risks voiding the resubmitted completion.   
• A TOR must never be sent until the device’s 30-second timeout has expired. 
• In the event a device has multiple queued up TOR transactions, the device must throttle the 
submission of these transactions, submitting no more than one every 30 seconds.   
• A TOR should only be sent during the same business day as the original transaction.

3-1 
3. Specifications Requirements 
This chapter provides information about the hardware, software, and telecommunications 
requirements necessary to support these specifications. 
A customer's host hardware and software must be capable of interfacing with BUYPASS 
hardware and software using a communications protocol that BUYPASS supports. 
3.1 Hardware Requirements 
Industry standard EFT processing hardware is supported by these specifications. 
Note: If a BUYPASS customer device supports any payment type that requires secure entry of 
a cardholder’s PIN, that device must be DUKPT-certified. 
3.2 Software Requirements 
Industry standard EFT processing software is supported by these specifications. 
If a vendor is a third-party processor, BUYPASS assigns a TPP (third party processor) ID or 
VAR (value added reseller) ID to the vendor.  Once this ID has been assigned, the vendor must 
send it to BUYPASS in the Variable Information (Element No. 113) of the Authorization Request.  
Also, please see valid entries in Appendix I.  Variable Information Data Layouts, Table ID 10 
(Visa® Trusted Agent Program Data) for additional information. 
A terminal ID must be assigned to each Point-of Sale (POS) entry point.  The terminal ID must 
be unique and the vendor must send it to BUYPASS in the Variable Information (Element No. 
113) of the Authorization Request.  Please see Appendix I.  Variable Information Data Layouts, 
Table ID 18 (Card Acceptor Terminal Identifier Information) for additional information. 
Note: Due to higher instances of fraud, it is highly recommended that the off-line/forced 
authorization key on the software/terminals be coded with a flag that will disable the key. The 
flag should be defaulted to off, so that the software/terminal does not have off-line/forced 
authorization key capability. The flag should be coded so that key can be enabled/disabled 
through setup within the software terminal.  
It is also recommended that a standalone password be added to the off-line/forced authorization 
key, so that when the key is enabled, the owner/manager has the capability to allow only certain 
personnel to perform the key function. The software/terminal should have the capability of 
changing the password independent of downloads and should not be linked to the default 
software/terminal passwords.

• Standard frame relay connection to multiple First Data data centers with dial backup 
• Any facility that emulates private leased lines, such as packet networks or satellite networks 
3.3.2 Dial Backup and Diverse Facilities 
BUYPASS supports and encourages merchant locations to implement dial backup facilities.  
Any location that generates more than 1,500 transactions per month must subscribe to dial 
backup.  Any location that generates more than 500,000 transactions per month must have at 
least two diverse connections that support automatic rerouting of traffic. 
The First Data standard requires that diverse connections use different carriers and are directed 
to two separate First Data data centers.  Transactions should be load-balanced across all 
connections.  BUYPASS directs responses over the same circuit as the initiating customer 
request.

6. PIN Encryption 
Key management involves the creation, distribution, maintenance, storage, and destruction of 
cryptographic keys.  This process is required between a customer's store device and the 
customer's host/device system, and between the customer's host/device system and 
BUYPASS. 
These specifications support the following PIN encryption methods: 
• DES 
• 3DES DUKPT 
This chapter discusses the following PIN encryption topics: 
• Requirements 
• 3DES DUKPT PIN Encryption Processing 
• DUKPT Derivation Key (DKey) 
• Key Sequence Number (KSN) 
• Test Key 
• PIN Block Construction 
• PIN Block Message Placement 
• Declines

6-2 
6.1 Requirements 
DUKPT PIN encryption (DUKPT) is the required PIN encryption method for BUYPASS 
processing. 
In addition, for effective key management, the following criteria must be met: 
• All personnel are excluded from handling keys in the clear except when performing an initial 
installation or when adding new or modifying existing customer store devices. 
• Personal identification numbers (PIN's) and cryptographic keys never appear in the clear. 
• PIN's and cryptographic keys are never retrievable by application programs. 
• For DUKPT PIN encryption, the customer devices and BUYPASS share the same derivation 
key (DKey).

6-3 
6.2 Triple DES (3DES) DUKPT PIN Encryption Processing 
This section contains the following information about Triple DES (3DES) DUKPT PIN encryption 
processing: 
• Customer PIN encryption 
• BUYPASS PIN encryption 
3DES DUKPT PIN encryption processing does not require the periodic exchange of PIN 
encryption keys as does master session PIN encryption processing.  This is accomplished by 
storing a 3DES DUKPT key at BUYPASS and using the 3DES DUKPT key to encrypt a serial 
number at each PIN pad. 
One 3DES DUKPT key exists between BUYPASS and a customer.  This means that potentially 
several hundred to several thousand PIN pads contain the same 3DES DUKPT key. 
A unique serial number is assigned to each PIN pad. 
The 3DES DUKPT key encrypts a PIN pad’s serial number; and the serial number and its 
encrypted form (seed key) are inserted in the assigned PIN pad. 
The seed key and its corresponding serial number can generate approximately one million 
unique PIN encryption keys. 
6.2.1 Customer PIN Encryption 
Hardware security modules must be used to encrypt all PIN’s, following ANSI® PIN 
management standards. 
Transmission of a PIN among interface participants must use DES-encrypted ANSI® PIN 
blocks. 
The following data are required to encrypt a PIN block for transmission to BUYPASS: 
• Card’s PAN 
• Cardholder’s PIN 
• Generated KPE 
6.2.1.1 Point-of-Entry PIN Encryption 
The following events occur to accomplish PIN encryption of a PIN block for transmission to the 
customer’s host system from the customer’s card reading device: 
1.  The PAN is read from the magnetic stripe card placed in the point-of-entry device by the 
cardholder.  Other information may be formatted on the card and can be read by the system. 
2. The point-of-entry device prompts the cardholder to enter his/her 4- to 12-digit PIN using a 
secure PIN pad. 
3. The PIN is encrypted with the generated KPE. 
4. The encrypted PIN block and the KSN are sent to the customer’s host system for forwarding 
to BUYPASS. 
--- PAGE 53 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
6-4 
6.2.2 BUYPASS PIN Encryption 
The following events occur to accomplish PIN encryption of the encrypted PIN block received 
from the customer’s host system by BUYPASS: 
1. The customer’s host system receives the encrypted PIN block and KSN from the point-of-
entry device. 
2. BUYPASS retrieves from its database the 3DES DUKPT key of the customer.  This key is 
encrypted under the BUYPASS master file key contained in the BUYPASS HSM. 
3. The encrypted PIN block, the PAN, the KSN, and the 3DES DUKPT key are passed to the 
BUYPASS HSM and translated into a new translated encrypted PIN block using the 
BUYPASS master key. 
4. The encrypted PIN block is translated in the BUYPASS HSM to a new translated PIN block 
using the network’s interchange working key. 
5. The encrypted PIN is transmitted to the network host system. 
6. The pathway terminal configuration for the PIN pad value must be defined for 3DES 
DUKPT. 
7. At the Bank FIID level the key representation for 3DES DUKPT must be defined.

 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications

6-5 
6.3 DUKPT Derivation Key (DKey) 
DUKPT uses a derivation key (DKey) and a key sequence number (KSN) to generate a unique 
PIN encryption key for every transaction that takes place at a PIN pad. 
The DKey is comprised of two 16-hexadecimal (HEX) character halves.  These halves are 
loaded onto the processor’s host and are associated with a given customer base.  When 
concatenated, these halves form a key part.  BUYPASS supports 2- and 3-part keys. 
6.4 Key Sequence Number (KSN) 
Another ingredient in the DUKPT algorithm is the key sequence number (KSN), which is a 20-
byte HEX field.  The format is discussed below. 
During the initialization process, the DKey and an initial key sequence number (IKSN) are used 
to create the base PIN encryption key.  Future PIN encryption keys for any PIN entry device are 
derived from the base PIN encryption key. 
The IKSN is 20 bytes but the right-most (low order) 4 bytes—the Transaction Counter—must be 
initialized to 0’s.  Each PIN-based transaction causes the KSN to increment. 
The key is changed at the PIN pad each time the KSN increments.  Because the same DKey is 
stored on the host and used in the injection of the PIN pad, the host is able to derive the PIN 
block in each transaction. 
The initial value of a 20-byte IKSN must follow the format below: 
PPPPXXXXXXXXXXEZ0000 
 Where: 
PPPP represents HEX characters (F’s); 
XXXXXXXXXX represents any 10-byte HEX character string; 
E represents any even HEX character (0, 2, C, E, etc.); 
Z represents zero; and 
0000 represents the Transaction Counter value. 
Note: The Transaction Counter can be manually included as part of the IKSN or 
programmatically concatenated by vendor-supplied software such as MKIXOR.

6-7 
6.7 PIN Block Message Placement 
The 16-byte PIN block in field no. 8 of the Standard Message Segment is followed by the KSN. 
The authorization message sent to BUYPASS contains a 16-byte encrypted PIN block and a 20-
byte KSN.  The host derives the PIN encryption based on the DKey stored at the host for the 
device associated with the transaction. 
6.8 Declines 
If a device receives either a 4R or 4< Decline Code while sending encrypted transactions to the 
host, one of the following situations may be the cause: 
• The encrypted PIN data is either not included in the format or not sent by the PIN encryption 
device. 
• The KSN is either missing or not sent by the PIN encryption device. 
• The KSN is not formatted correctly. 
• The Terminal Profile PIN Encryption type is not set to UKP. 
• The PIN pad is encrypted incorrectly. 
• The KSN counter is not incrementing for each PIN transaction. 
• The KSN is not the correct length. 
• The BANK FIID is incorrect.

the day, along with the Totals Report.

8.1.3 Automated Fuel Pump Controller System Activities  
The following table describes, in sequential order, the activities performed by the customer’s 
AFP controller system during transaction processing: 
Notes: If the controller does not receive a Transaction Response from the host, it should 
generate a Local Approval Response. 
If the DLL flag is set in a host response message, the controller connects to BUYPASS and 
requests a PIN encryption load once the queue is empty. 
AFP Controller System Activities 
Step No.  Description 
1. Before pumping fuel, the customer completes the following tasks: 
• Selects card type 
• Swipes/inserts card 
• Enters PIN (required for debit and some fleet cards) 
• Enters additional fields (determined by card type) 
• Select product (optional) 
2. The island device/controller must verify the following card data when applicable: 
• ISO number 
• Expiration data 
• Check digit calculation 
• Card range 
3. The island device/controller should also validate the following card data: 
• Account number 
• Purchase amount 
• Card issuer 
4. The controller formats the data into a Preauthorization Request.  The format must 
indicate that the transaction was initiated by a customer-activated device. 
5. The controller supplies the Preauthorization amount, the anticipated fuel type, and 
the price per gallon.  This is overridden when the actual fuel is dispensed but is 
required for fuel limits and fuel-only card validation. 
6. The controller connects to BUYPASS if not already connected. 
7. The controller forwards the Authorization Only Request. 
8. The controller parses the Authorization Only Response, storing the transaction 
data and approval code if the transaction is approved. 
9. The controller signals the island device of the approval or decline. 
10. If an approval is received, the island device signals the AFP system to dispense 
the fuel up to the preapproved Preauthorization amount. 
11. The controller services any Authorization Requests subsequently initiated if the 
controller is still connected to BUYPASS and the line disconnect timer has not 
expired. 
12. If the controller is still connected to BUYPASS, the controller forwards any queued 
transactions (preauthorization completions), parses the responses, and updates 
associated electronic journal data.

8-4 
AFP Controller System Activities 
Step No.  Description 
13. If the controller is still connected to BUYPASS, no transactions are pending, and 
the load request flag is set to yes, request the load before hanging up the line. 
14. After the fuel is pumped, the island device stores the following information: 
• Actual purchase amount 
• Fuel price per gallon 
• Fuel type 
• Gallons dispensed to the controller 
A receipt is printed reflecting the actual purchase amount. 
For debit and stored value cards, the transaction can only be stored for a 
maximum of fifteen minutes, and then the controller must connect to BUYPASS for 
processing the transaction. 
For credit cards, the transaction can only be stored for a maximum of 55 minutes, 
and then the controller must connect to BUYPASS for processing the transaction. 
For all other card types, this transaction should be stored until the next 
Authorization or other request that initiates a connection to BUYPASS.  A stored 
preauthorized completion transaction should never initiate a connection to 
BUYPASS. 
15. Prior to requesting end-of-day totals, all queued transactions, including the Daily 
Exception Log transactions, should be sent to BUYPASS.  The device should 
connect to BUYPASS 15 minutes prior to the cut time if the location has not 
processed its totals.

8-5 
8.2 Restaurant and Lodging Processing Overview 
The BUYPASS restaurant and lodging interfaces provide controller-based systems with the 
ability to communicate with BUYPASS in order to request authorizations for restaurant and 
lodging purchases and draft capture of restaurant and lodging purchases. 
Restaurant Credit card sales are terminal-capture and initiated as POS Authorization Only 
transactions.  Transactions are stored in the terminal batch as pending transactions until they 
have (or have not) been adjusted for tips.  Tip adjustments are completed offline at the terminal.  
When the batch is closed, the pending sales are marked to send and uploaded as POS 
Purchase/Capture transactions, including the approval number from the original transaction 
request.  A Totals Request (999999 – Shift Read and Reset) follows the successful completion 
of a batch upload.  If a communication error occurs during the batch upload, the terminal 
reconnects to the host and follows normal TOR logic for any sent transactions that have not 
received an ACK from the host.  The terminal then sends only the remaining transactions in the 
batch and does not resend transactions that have already received an ACK.  An exception 
report prints after a successful batch upload.  It includes any transactions declined during the 
upload process. 
Restaurant Debit, EBT, and gift sales are host-capture and initiated as POS Purchase/Capture 
transactions.  Transactions prompt for tips at the time of the sale.  Tip adjustment is not allowed 
with these card types. 
At the completion of the business day, the terminal sends a Totals Request (222222 – Read 
and Cut Settlement) after sending the last batch.

9-2 
9.1 Electronic Journal 
Note: An electronic journal feature is not provided by BUYPASS; however, it can be designed, 
created, and implemented by a BUYPASS customer.  The information in this section 
provides an example of how an electronic journal can be designed and used. 
In this example an electronic journal needs to contain all approved transactions, excluding 
authorization only transactions.  Also, local totals need to be an accumulation of the 
transactions in the electronic journal, including authorization only transactions.  The electronic 
journal and local totals features are separate functions for this example, and the local totals are 
calculated from the electronic journal. 
In this example an electronic journal provides a listing of each approved transaction for local 
review.  When the host response to an approved transaction is received, the customer device—
in this example a device—immediately records the transaction in the electronic journal.  The 
electronic journal is structured as a circular queue.  It can be accessed by a designated key for 
each device type. 
In this example, the following data for each transaction should be stored in an electronic journal: 
• Account Number 
• Card Type 
• Manual slide indicator 
• Transaction day (1–31) 
• Transaction time (HH:MM) 
• Total transaction amount 
• Transaction type (approval, reversal, or merchandise return) 
• Approval Number 
• Sequence Number

9-13 
9.3 Host Totals 
This section discusses the activities involved in requesting host totals from BUYPASS. 
The device must be able to support all requests for merchant shift totals and settlement totals. 
When requesting host totals, the device displays a prompt for entering a password and date.  The 
password must match the data in the BUYPASS merchant profile that is obtained via a Table 
Load.  The host totals are accessed by entering a 6-digit Totals Date code (Please see chapter 13, 
“Data Element Descriptions,” for a list of valid codes for Element No. 105, Totals Date.) 
BUYPASS maintains two sets of daily totals for each merchant: 
• Shift totals 
• Settlement totals 
9.3.1 Merchant Shift Totals 
This section discusses the activities involved in requesting merchant shift totals from BUYPASS. 
Shift totals accumulate for each merchant from work shift to work shift.  These totals are scratch 
totals and do not affect settlement.  They can accumulate beyond a merchant’s cut time.  These 
totals can be requested as read only or read and reset.  Descriptions of both of these total requests 
follow, together with their respective 6-digit Totals Date codes. 
9.3.1.1 Read Only Total Request 
To request shift totals as read only, enter the following 6-digit Totals Date code in the date field 
displayed on the device:  111111. 
Entering this code enables a merchant to view shift totals without resetting the BUYPASS shift total 
amounts to zero.  BUYPASS returns the host shift totals for transactions done since the last shift 
cut [Read and Reset Total Request (Totals Date code:  999999)]. 
9.3.1.2 Read and Reset Total Request 
To request shift totals as read and reset, enter the following 6-digit Totals Date code in the date 
field displayed on the device:  999999. 
Entering this code enables a merchant to view shift totals and reset the BUYPASS shift total 
amounts to zero.  BUYPASS returns the host shift totals for transactions done since the last shift 
cut [Read and Reset Total Request (Totals Date code:  999999)], ends the current shift, and resets 
the merchant shift total amounts to zero. 
Use these totals to balance against the local totals stored in the merchant’s device.  If the merchant 
fails to request shift totals at the end of a shift, the totals continue to accumulate at BUYPASS until 
a Read and Reset Total Request (Totals Date code:  999999) is made.  The host maintains the 
shift totals and they are available until the first transaction in a new shift has been completed.  This 
allows retrieval of the shift totals from the most recently completed shift. 
--- PAGE 76 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications

Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
9-14 
9.3.2 Settlement Totals 
Settlement totals accumulate over a 24-hour period and are totaled once a day.  The settlement 
time, also known as the cut time, is determined by the merchant. 
The merchant chooses a default settlement time and has the option of cutting totals before that 
time.  A merchant exercising this option is referred to as a variable-cut merchant. 
Settlement totals can be requested as read only or read and cut.  Descriptions of both of these total 
requests follow, together with their respective 6-digit Totals Date codes. 
Business day totals can be requested as read only for the current business day, the previous 
business day, or the business day before the previous business day.  Descriptions of these total 
requests follow, together with their respective 6-digit Totals Date codes. 
9.3.2.1 Read Only Settlement Totals Request 
To request settlement totals for a specific business day as read only, enter the desired 6-character 
settlement date in the date field displayed on the device in the following format:  MMDDYY. 
Entering this specific date enables a merchant to view settlement totals for a specific date without 
resetting the BUYPASS settlement total amounts to zero.  BUYPASS returns the host settlement 
totals for transactions that settle on the specified date. 
Using the Totals Date code of MMDDYY returns totals for transactions that settled on the specified 
date. 
Note: Settlement Date refers to the date when transactions actually settle.  Unless the 
merchant chooses to end the business day at 2:00 p.m., settlement time does not 
coincide with the BUYPASS end-of-business day.  In most cases, to retrieve totals for a 
current business day, request totals using a settlement date equivalent to the business 
day plus one day. 
Based on the merchant-selected end-of-business daytime, BUYPASS groups all transactions done 
in that 24-hour period and totals them; however, BUYPASS does not run a settlement until 2:00 
p.m.  Therefore, if the merchant’s end-of-day is 6:00 p.m., transactions for that day settle at 2:00 
p.m. on the following day. 
9.3.2.2 Read and Cut Settlement Totals Request 
This option can be used only by variable-cut merchants. 
To request totals for the current settlement date as read and cut, enter the following 6-digit Totals 
Date code in the date field displayed on the device:  222222. 
Entering this code enables a variable-cut merchant to close its business day before the 
predetermined cut time as designated on the BUYPASS merchant profile.  If the variable-cut  
  
--- PAGE 77 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
9-15 
merchant does not request read and cut totals, BUYPASS automatically closes the merchant's 
business day at the designated cut time.  Transactions performed after close of business are 
included in the next business day's totals. 
Notes: In a controller-based automated fuel pump environment, the controller should be 
designed to connect to BUYPASS 30 minutes before the designated cut time and 
forward all queued trailer transactions to the host.  This ensures that all authorization 
only/preauthorization transaction pairs are captured on the same business day.  After all 
trailer transactions are transmitted to BUYPASS, the controller completes a read and cut

 If a device supports table loads from BUYPASS, receiving the Card Type (Element No. 14)

9.3.2.3 Current Business Day Read Only Total Request 
To request settlement totals for the current business day as read only, enter the following 6-digit 
Totals Date code in the date field displayed on the device:  333333. 
Entering this code enables a merchant to view up-to-date current business day totals. 
Note: Using this code produces the same result as following the instructions for using the 
Read Only Settlement Totals Request described in section 9.3.2.1, “Read Only 
Settlement Totals Request.” 
9.3.2.4 Previous Business Day Read Only Total Request 
To request settlement totals for the previous business day as read only, enter the following 6-digit 
Totals Date code in the date field displayed on the device:  444444. 
Entering this code enables a merchant to view the previous business day’s totals. 
Note: It is possible for calendar days to elapse between business days.  For example, if a 
Previous Business Day Read Only Total Request is made on a Monday, and there were 
no transactions done the preceding Saturday and Sunday, totals are returned for the 
previous Friday. 
9.3.2.5 Business Day Before Previous Business Day Cut Total Request 
To request settlement totals for the business day before the previous business day (the third most 
recent business day), enter the following 6-digit Totals Date code in the date field displayed on the 
device:  555555. 
Entering this code enables a merchant to view the totals for the business day before the previous 
business day. 
Note: It is possible for calendar days to elapse between business days.  For example, if a 
Business Day Before Previous Business Day Cut Total Request is made on a Monday, 
and there were no transactions done the preceding Saturday and Sunday, totals are 
returned for the previous Thursday.

10.1 Credit Card Processing Requirements 
This section discusses the following credit card processing requirements: 
• Card requirements 
• Supported transaction types 
• Partial Approval transaction 
• Authorization Only Reversal transaction 
• Address Verification Service 
• Bill payment/Recurring and Installment payment transactions 
• Radio frequency identification (RFID) service 
• Healthcare auto-substantiation service 
• Receipt requirements 
• Regulatory requirements 
10.1.1 Card Requirements 
This section discusses the following card requirements for credit card processing: 
• Expiration date 
• Track support 
• Manual entry 
10.1.1.1 Expiration Date 
The device performs expiration date validation in a credit card transaction. 
Note: Dates up to and including December, 2049 (Format:  1249) are assumed to be in the 
twenty-first century. 
10.1.1.2 Track Support 
The default track that is sent to the host should be Track 2 if the device supports Track 2.  If the 
device cannot read Track 2, then the device should send unaltered Track 1 before attempting 
manual entry. If a Pre-Auth transaction is approved offline, the full track data must be sent. Also 
if a Sale transaction is approved offline, the full track data must be sent. 
Note: Track 1 data is mandatory for all (both MSR and MSD) Amex AFD transactions and 
preferred for all other Amex transactions. 
If the AFD transaction being submitted contains encrypted data in the TransArmor 
Encryption Block, Track 1 data must be present inside the Encryption Block with 
Encryption Target as Track 1. 
For all other card types, the default track should be Track 2.  If the device cannot read 
Track 2, then the device should send unaltered Track 1 on the initial transaction, before 
attempting manual entry. 
All follow-up transactions should use truncated Track 2 or truncated Track 2 facsimile. 
 
10.1.1.3 Manual Entry 
Manual entry is allowed on a credit card transaction.  If the device is unable to read the card's 
magnetic strip, it should prompt the user to swipe the card again—up to three times.  If unable 
to read the magnetic strip after three attempts, the device should prompt for manual entry of the 
Account Number and Expiration Date (Format:  MMYY). 
Note: If manual entry is used, this fact is indicated on the receipt and journal by an asterisk (*) 
before the Account Number.

10.1.2.1 Partial Approval Transaction 
A Partial Approval transaction enables a merchant to receive approval for the amount available 
on the presented credit card when the account balance is more or less than the amount of the 
Transaction Request. 
Credit networks supporting the Partial Approval transaction return an approval containing the 
following information: 
Note: This information is returned when a Partial Approval Indicator value of 1 is sent in Partial 
Approval Indicator (Element No. 121). 
• A Response Code (Element No. 83) value of F (Indicates “approval, partial amount 
approved.”) 
• Approved Amount (Element No. 6) contains the approved partial amount, and the POS 
device must prompt for payment of the remaining balance due on the sale. 
• The card balance—if returned by the issuer—is in the Additional Information Data Segment 
(Segment No. 112). 
Partial Approval transactions are supported for: 
• POS Purchase 
• POS Authorization Only 
• CAT Authorization Only 
The amount in a Reversal (Void) request must be the amount approved in the original 
transaction response when a transaction has been partially approved. BUYPASS supports 
reversal of a partially approved original authorization and NOT a partial reversal of an original 
transaction. 
The amount in a TOR request must be the amount requested in the original transaction 
response when a transaction has been partially approved. 
The Sequence Number must be the Sequence Number contained in the original transaction 
request.

 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications

10-6 
10.1.2.2 Authorization Only Reversal Transaction 
In support of the following requirements, BUYPASS supports the Authorization Only Reversal 
transaction: 
• All approved and partially approved authorization transactions must be either cleared or 
reversed. 
• Acquirers must ensure that their merchants process authorization reversals for 
authorizations submitted in error and/or cardholder cancelled card-present transactions 
within 24 hours.  Card-absent merchants are allowed up to 72 hours to process the required 
partial or full authorization reversals. 
• Issuers must immediately process matched reversal transactions, subject to the issuer’s risk 
or fraud control policies, and release any applicable holds on cardholder available funds. 
• It is recommended for merchants who use velocity processing to send the SIC Information 
Code (Data Segment 111, Table ID 007) of “5542” for CAT (outside) transactions and 
“5541” for inside transactions. 
This transaction enables a merchant to reverse the following credit card transactions within 
required timeframes: 
• POS Authorization Only (Transaction Type code “3”) 
• CAT Authorization Only (Transaction Type code “5”) 
Successful reversal matching requires the following: 
• Element No. 5 (Approval Number)—present in the original transaction—must be present 
and identical in the Authorization Only Reversal transaction. 
• Element No.86 (Sequence Number)—present in the original transaction—must be present 
and identical in the Authorization Only Reversal transaction. 
• Element No. 78 (Prompt Code) must contain a Transaction Type code “S” to indicate 
cancellation.

10-7 
10.1.3 Address Verification Service 
Address Verification Service (AVS) is a credit card authorization tool used for transactions 
performed primarily in a non-face-to-face environment, such as mail order, phone order, or 
customer-activated terminal (CAT). 
The device sends a transaction request to BUYPASS containing the AVS information in the 
Variable Information Data Segment (Please refer to sections 11.1, “Financial Transactions,” and 
12.10, “Variable Information Data Segment,” for additional information.). 
The authorizer returns a response containing both the transaction authorization Response Code 
and the AVS information in the Additional Information Data Segment (Please refer to sections 
11.1, “Financial Transactions,” and 12.11, “Additional Information Data Segment," for additional 
information.). 
BUYPASS processes all Purchase/Capture transactions when the Response Code is an 
approval, regardless of the AVS information.  If the merchant decides not to accept the 
purchase due to the value of the AVS information, the merchant must perform a Purchase 
Reversal. 
10.1.4 Bill Payment/Recurring and Installment Payment 
Transactions 
Support for bill payment/recurring and installment payment transactions is an optional service.  
These transactions must be identified by a Variable Information Indicator located in the Variable 
Information section of the Variable Information Data Segment (Segment No. 111).  (See section 
12.10, “Variable Information Data Segment.”) 
10.1.5 Radio Frequency Identification Service 
Radio frequency identification (RFID) service is an optional service.  It is a contactless data 
transmission and capture technology.  When applied to credit card processing, it refers to the 
capability of a point-of-sale device to capture and transmit full, unaltered Track 2 data from a 
card without requiring the card to have contact with the point-of-sale device. 
An RFID card has a chip embedded in the card that transmits Track 2 data wirelessly when the 
card is in close proximity to an RFID receiver.  Most RFID cards also have a magnetic stripe on 
the back of the card that can be used with a card reader if an RFID receiver is not present. 
RFID processing requires that the appropriate values be sent in Point-of-Sale Entry Mode 
(Contained in Element No. 113, Variable Information.) on all transactions when an RFID receiver 
is connected to the point-of-sale device or controller.  Even if the transaction is swiped, 
manually keyed, or uses a card type for which RFID is not applicable, Point-of-Sale Entry Mode 
must be populated correctly in the transaction request from the point-of-sale when an RFID 
receiver is present.

10.1.6 Healthcare Auto-Substantiation Service 
The Healthcare Auto-Substantiation Service provided by credit card issuers (Amex®, Discover® 
Network, MasterCard®, Visa®) and PIN debit card issuers, is supported by these specifications. 
This service identifies and substantiates medical purchases, including over-the-counter (OTC) 
purchases, for flexible spending accounts (FSA) and health reimbursement arrangement (HRA) 
accounts. 
This section discusses the following FSA/HRA card processing requirements: 
• Card requirements 
• Transaction Request requirements 
• Transaction Response requirements 
• Supported transaction types 
• Receipt requirements 
10.1.6.1 Card Requirements 
This section discusses the following card requirements for FSA/HRA card processing: 
• Eligible benefit cards 
• Partial Approval 
• Split tender processing 
• Qualified healthcare products 
10.1.6.1.1 Eligible Benefit Cards 
Eligible benefit cards are identified by a 9-digit BIN.  The merchant’s POS system must be able 
to store BIN information for use at the time the card is swiped at the device. 
10.1.6.1.2 Partial Approval 
If Partial Approvals are not supported, the transaction request will either be approved for the full 
amount, or the transaction will be declined. 
10.1.6.1.3 Split Tender Processing 
A Split Tender transaction results when a Partial Approval is returned to the POS in the 
transaction response.  The POS device must then prompt for payment of the remaining balance 
due on the sale.  The cardholder uses a different form of payment for nonqualified items, such 
as another payment card, cash, or a check.

• Purchase Reversal 
• Merchandise Return

response when a transaction has been partially approved. 
The Sequence Number must be the Sequence Number contained in the original transaction

10.1.7.4 Account Number 
The Account Number (Element No. 2) must be truncated—suppressed to its last four digits—on 
all transaction receipts. 
A series of X's equal to the number of suppressed digits precedes these last four digits for a 
field length equal to the original Account Number length. 
Example.  The Account Number 1234567890123456 prints as:  XXXXXXXXXXXX3456. 
The full Account Number can be retrievable from the terminal journal or transaction log for 
retrieval requests. 
Note: If manual entry is used, this fact is indicated on the receipt and journal by an asterisk (*) 
before the Account Number. 
10.1.7.5 Expiration Date 
The Expiration Date is the expiration date of the card presented in a transaction. 
The Expiration Date must be suppressed on all transaction receipts. 
10.1.7.6 Transaction Date 
The date of the transaction prints on all credit card receipts. 
10.1.7.7 Transaction Time 
The time of the transaction prints on all credit card receipts. 
10.1.7.8 Sequence Number 
The transaction's Sequence Number appears on all credit card receipts. 
10.1.7.9 Product Information 
The following product information must appear on a receipt for an "approved" transaction: 
• Fuel product information 
 Fuel type 
 Quantity in gallons 
 Price per gallon 
 Total fuel purchase amount 
• Nonfuel product information 
 Number of units of product 
 Unit price of product 
 Total product purchase amount 
10.1.7.10 Balance Information 
Balance information prints on a credit card receipt for a Partial Approval transaction and a 
Balance Return with Purchase transaction.  In these cases, the available card balance prints on 
an approved or declined transaction receipt when that amount is returned in the transaction 
response.  This pertains to transactions in which an available card balance is returned by the 
issuer to the POS device.

10.1.8 Regulatory Requirements 
This section discusses the following regulatory requirements that must be met when processing 
all electronic credit (American Express®, Diners Club®, Discover® Network, JCB®, 
MasterCard®, MasterCard® Fleet, Visa®, and Visa® Fleet) transactions: 
• Data storage requirements 
• Track support requirements 
10.1.8.1 Data Storage Requirements 
The following data storage requirements must be met when processing all electronic credit 
transactions: 
• A device at the point of interaction must not display/store any card-read data except the 
card’s account number, card’s expiration date, and cardholder’s name, if present. 
• The merchant device must not store full magnetic stripe data. 
• The merchant—or any agent representative thereof—may record only the card’s account 
number, card’s expiration date, and cardholder’s name on paper, microfiche, or an online 
authorization file, for research purposes at its site.  This data must be kept and maintained 
in a secure manner. 
• Full card-read data (including discretionary data) must not be stored.  The merchant—or any 
agent or representative thereof—must not record, store, replicate, or use full card-read data 
for any other purpose.  By way of example—but not limited to—card data provided in an 
authorization or clearing transaction must not be the result of previously captured full card-
read data. 
10.1.8.2 Track Support Requirements 
The following track support requirements must be met when processing all electronic credit 
transactions: 
• The default track that is sent to the host should be Track 2 if the device supports Track 2.  If 
the device cannot read Track 2, then the device should send unaltered Track 1 before 
attempting manual entry. 
Note: For American Express, the default track should be Track 1.  If the device cannot read 
Track 1, then the device should send unaltered Track 2 on the initial transaction, before 
attempting manual entry. 
• Regulatory requirements regarding data storage dictate that full card-read data (including 
discretionary data) must not be stored. 
• Card data provided in a clearing transaction must not be the result of previously captured full 
card-read data.   
Note: This does not apply to the TransArmor-Verifone Edition processing. 
The host message should only contain the following card data information in the Account 
Number and Card Discretionary Block Data fields: 
 Account Number 
 Expiration Date (Field format:  YYMM) 
Note: These two items must be separated by an “=” sign, rather than a Field Separator.  
(Please see Processing Rules for Card Discretionary Block Data (Element No. 12) in 
chapter 13, “Data Element Descriptions,” for additional information.) 
• The host message should only contain the Account Number, followed by an account 
delimiter (=), followed by the 4 digit Expiration Date (Storage format – YYMM).  No other 
--- PAGE 93 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-16 
Card Discretionary Data field follows the 4-digit Expiration Date.  This scenario applies only 
to the following credit transactions: 
 Credit Completions 
 Credit POS Purchase Reversals 
 Credit Time Out Reversals       
 Credit POS Cancellations 
 Credit Cancellations         
There is one exception to these track support requirements: 
• In Flight Table 
• Track 2 data is kept in this table while the transaction is in process.  It is removed from the 
table when the transaction is completed. 
Note: All offline transactions must send full unaltered track data. This includes both Track 1

10.2 Debit Card Processing Requirements 
This section discusses the following debit card processing requirements: 
• Card requirements 
• Supported transaction types 
• Healthcare auto-substantiation service 
• Receipt requirements 
• Regulatory requirements 
10.2.1 Card Requirements 
This section discusses the following card requirements for debit card processing: 
• Expiration date 
• Duplicate Completion transactions 
• PIN entry 
• Manual entry 
10.2.1.1 Expiration Date 
The device does not perform expiration date validation on a debit card when the card is 
processed as a debit transaction.  On-line authorization must be requested for the transaction 
regardless of the expiration date on the card. 
10.2.1.2 Duplicate Completion Transactions 
When processing a Debit Card Completion transaction, the transaction can only be processed 
one time by BUYPASS and debit networks.  This transaction cannot be reversed or processed 
again by the device. 
In the event the device sends a Debit Card Completion transaction to BUYPASS and does not 
receive a response, the device should resend the request on the next dial attempt or 30 minutes 
later—whichever occurs first.  If the device receives a Response Code value of 1 (indicating a 
"decline") and a Decline Code value of 24 in the transaction response message, then the device 
should treat the response as already captured on BUYPASS and update the device totals as 
"approved." 
Any response from BUYPASS to a Debit Card Completion transaction should end attempts to 
retry a Debit Card Completion whether "approved" or "declined." 
10.2.1.3 PIN Entry 
When processing a debit card transaction, the entry of the customer PIN is required on a DES-
compliant entry device, and it must be encrypted using the DUKPT PIN encryption method. 
All transactions—except the Purchase Reversal transaction—require PIN entry. 
10.2.1.4 Manual Entry 
Manual entry is not allowed on a debit card transaction.  If the device is unable to read the 
card's magnetic strip, it should prompt the user to swipe the card again—up to three times.  If 
unable to read the magnetic strip after three attempts, a message should be displayed to the 
clerk and the transaction ended.

10.2.2 Supported Transaction Types 
The following point-of-sale transactions are supported for debit card processing: 
• Purchase/Capture 
• Purchase with Cashback 
• Purchase Reversal 
• Authorization Only 
• Merchandise Return 
• Time-out Reversal

• Void of a Merchandise Return 
• Balance Inquiry

The following customer-activated transactions are supported for debit card processing: 
• Purchase/Capture 
• Authorization Only 
• Time-out Reversal 
• Partial Approval 
• Authorization Only Reversal 
10.2.2.1 Partial Approval Transaction 
A Partial Approval transaction enables a merchant to receive approval for a PIN debit card’s 
balance if that balance is more or less than the transaction request amount. 
Debit networks supporting the Partial Approval transaction return an approval containing the 
following information: 
Note: This information is returned when a Partial Approval Indicator value of 1 is sent in Partial 
Approval Indicator (Element No. 121). 
• A Response Code (Element No. 83) value of F (Indicates “approval, partial amount 
approved.”) 
• Approved Amount (Element No. 6) contains the approved partial amount, and the POS 
device must prompt for payment of the remaining balance due on the sale. 
• The card balance—if returned by the issuer—is in the Additional Information Data Segment 
(Segment No. 112). 
Partial Approval transactions are supported for: 
• POS Purchase 
• POS Purchase with Cashback 
• POS Authorization Only 
• CAT Authorization Only 
Note: As of April, 2013, Interlink requires that merchants supporting cashback must also 
support Partial Approval transactions.  Most merchants support Partial Approval transactions as 
part of a previous Maestro mandate.  This note is to clarify that merchants supporting cashback 
must also support Partial Approval transactions.  Merchants must ensure that their systems 
allow for this mandate. If any debit transaction requesting authorization for purchase with

cashback is partially approved, then the partially approved amount will be for the purchase only 
and not cashback. 
The amount in a Reversal (Void) request must be the amount approved in the original 
transaction response when a transaction has been partially approved. 
The amount in a TOR request must be the amount approved in the original transaction

10.2.2.2 Authorization Only Reversal Transaction 
In support of the following requirements, BUYPASS supports the Authorization Only Reversal 
transaction: 
• All approved and partially approved authorization transactions must be either cleared or 
reversed. 
• Acquirers must ensure that their merchants process authorization reversals for 
authorizations submitted in error and/or cardholder cancelled card-present transactions 
within 24 hours.  Card-absent merchants are allowed up to 72 hours to process the required 
partial or full authorization reversals. 
• Issuers must immediately process matched reversal transactions, subject to the issuer’s risk 
or fraud control policies, and release any applicable holds on cardholder available funds. 
This transaction enables a merchant to reverse the following debit card transactions within 
required timeframes: 
• POS Authorization Only (Transaction Type code “3”) 
• CAT Authorization Only (Transaction Type code “5”) 
Successful reversal matching requires the following: 
• Element No. 5 (Approval Number)—present in the original transaction—must be present 
and identical in the Authorization Only Reversal transaction. 
• Element No.86 (Sequence Number)—present in the original transaction—must be present 
and identical in the Authorization Only Reversal transaction. 
• Element No. 78 (Prompt Code) must contain a Transaction Type code “S” to indicate 
cancellation.

purchases, for flexible spending accounts (FSA) and health reimbursement arrangement (HRA)

10.3 PINless POS Debit Card Processing Requirements 
Note: Please check with your First Data Relationship Manager for the availability of this 
functionality. 
This section discusses the following PINless POS Debit card processing requirements: 
• Card requirements 
• Supported transaction types 
10.3.1 Card Requirements 
PINless POS Debit cards allow certain POS Debit transactions to be processed without a PIN. 
Card requirements for PINless POS Debit card processing include the following: 
• Card must be issued by a supported Debit network 
• For MSR, Card must be swiped at a POS device 
• For EMV, the card may be dipped or tapped for contact or contactless transactions 
Note: For EMV, POS PINless transactions are ONLY eligible with the US Common Debit AID 
as ‘No CVM’ and ‘No PIN Block’. 
• Card Track Data must be Track 2 
10.3.2 Supported Transaction Types 
The following point-of-sale transactions are supported for PINless POS Debit card processing: 
• Purchase 
• Merchandise Return\Refund 
• Time-out Reversal (TOR) 
Note: A Time-out Reversal (TOR) transaction is used to reverse a transaction on one of the 
following occasions: 
• If the POS device fails. 
• If the transaction is aborted after initial communication with the host. 
Supported transactions do not require a PIN when less than or equal to $50.00. The PINless 
POS feature has been expanded to support over $50.00 for Non-PIN debit transactions 
(PINless POS Plus product) for specific BINs of debit networks. 
Note: The amount may be updated as required by debit networks. 
The following exclusions are applicable for PINless POS Debit transactions: 
• Transactions with cashback 
• Healthcare (FSA) transactions. HSA is not excluded, since they are treated as prepaid cards 
• Automated Fuel Dispenser (MCC 5542) transactions 
• Transactions where the final amount is not known (restaurant with tip, hotels, car rental) 
• Store and Forward transactions

10.4.1 Card Requirements 
Signature Debit cards allow certain debit transactions to be processed without a PIN. Card 
requirements for Signature Debit card processing include the following: 
• Card must be issued by a supported debit network 
• Card must support all entry modes, such as, manual, swiped, contact chip, and contactless 
chip  
 
Note: STAR® is a debit network that is expanding its transaction set to support Signature Debit 
in addition to its current support of PIN and PINless debit. This expansion may provide 
additional routing choices for merchants. This new offering will allow merchants in most 
processing environments the ability to take advantage of the various cardholder verification 
methods, i.e. PIN, signature, etc., available for the transaction based on a merchant’s chosen 
point-of-sale device. Please contact your Account Manager for additional information. 
10.4.2 Supported Transaction Types 
The following point-of-sale transactions are supported for Signature Debit card processing: 
• Purchase/Capture 
• Purchase Reversal 
• Authorization Only 
• Time-out Reversal 
• Authorization Only Cancellation 
• Partial Approval 
Note: A Time-out Reversal (TOR) transaction is used to reverse a transaction on one of the 
following occasions: 
• If the POS device fails 
• If the transaction is aborted after initial communication with the host 
 
10.4.3 Restrictions for Processing STAR® Single and Dual 
Message 
The following are the BUYPASS Platform restrictions to process STAR Single and Dual 
message: 
• Transactions processed as STAR Signature Debit must occur within US and US territories 
(Guam, Puerto Rico, Virgin Islands etc.) 
• The transaction must be settled only in US Dollar (840) 
• Cash back is not supported 
• Recharge, Activate, or Inquiry transactions are not supported 
• eCommerce transactions, including those using 3-D Secure Protocol, such as Verified by 
Visa, MC Secure code transactions, Amex SafeKey and Discover ProtectBuy are not 
supported 
10.4.4 Additional Restrictions for Processing STAR® Single 
Message 
Besides the restrictions listed in the above section, STAR Single message processing has the 
following additional restrictions: 
• The transactions must be card present, full mag-stripe data, or full EMV chip data.

10.5 Electronic Benefits Transfer Card Processing 
Requirements 
This section discusses the following electronic benefits transfer (EBT) card processing 
requirements: 
• Card requirements 
• Food stamp electronic vouchers 
• Supported transaction types 
• Receipt requirements 
• eWIC transaction processing 
• Healthy Incentives Program (HIP) Transaction Processing 
10.5.1 Card Requirements 
This section discusses the following card requirements for EBT card processing: 
• Expiration date 
• PIN entry 
• Manual entry 
• Stand-in mode 
• Tender types 
• Balance inquiry 
10.5.1.1 Expiration Date 
The device does not perform expiration date validation in an EBT card transaction. 
10.5.1.2 PIN Entry 
All transactions—except the Food Stamp Electronic Voucher transaction, Food Stamp Reversal 
(Void) transaction, and Cash Benefit Reversal (Void) transaction—require PIN entry. 
10.5.1.3 Manual Entry 
Manual entry of EBT must be supported; however, the store’s device must prompt for the PIN 
regardless of Account Number entry mode. 
For manually entered Account Numbers, the device must also prompt for the card’s expiration 
date. If no expiration date is provided, use 1249. 
10.5.1.4 Stand-in Mode 
Currently, there is no "stand-in" mode for EBT transactions.  The USDA guidelines do not 
specifically allow for the off-line processing of EBT transactions.  In addition, a defined 
transaction format that supports stored-and-forwarded (SAF) EBT transactions does not exist.  If 
the retailer chooses to support SAF EBT transactions, the retailer assumes all risk for 
transactions submitted once the connection is reestablished.  The PIN must be stored in an 
encrypted format.  The balance field must not print on the receipt (Do not print zeros.). 
10.5.1.5 Tender Types 
EBT processing supports the following tender types: 
• Food stamps 
• Cash benefits

10.5.2 Food Stamp Electronic Vouchers 
Electronic vouchers electronically submit food stamp approvals received over the phone during 
a device, BUYPASS, or authorizing host outage.  Electronic vouchers must prompt for the 
following items: 
• Account Number prompt 
• Approval Number prompt 
• Voucher Number prompt 
10.5.2.1 Account Number Prompt 
If the store system can retain the account information from an original transaction attempt, the 
remainder of the information can be entered at the controller level or directly into the device in 
the lane.  For stand-alone equipment, the electronic voucher transaction must allow for manual 
entry of the Account Number and the Expiration Date. 
In cases where the PAN is printed on transaction receipts, it must be truncated to its last four 
digits.  A series of X's equal to the number of truncated digits precede these four digits for a field 
length equal to the original Account Number's length. 
Example.  The Account Number 1234567890123456 prints as XXXXXXXXXXXX3456. 
10.5.2.2 Approval Number Prompt 
The device must allow for entry of the Approval Number received over the phone. 
10.5.2.3 Voucher Number Prompt 
The device must allow for entry of the Voucher Number from the manual voucher ticket. 
10.5.3 Supported Transaction Types 
The following transaction types are supported for EBT processing: 
• Food Stamp Purchase 
• Food Stamp Reversal (Void) 
• Food Stamp Return 
• Cash Benefit Purchase 
• Cash Benefit Reversal (Void) 
• Food Stamp Balance Inquiry 
• Food Stamp Electronic Voucher 
• Cash Benefit Purchase with Cash Back 
• Cash Benefit Balance Inquiry 
• Time-out Reversal 
• Food Stamp Void of a Merchandise Return

10.5.4 Receipt Requirements 
The credit card receipt requirements listed in section 10.1.7, "Receipt Requirements," also apply 
to EBT card receipts with the exception of Approved/Declined Message. 
In addition to those requirements, the following information must appear on EBT card receipts: 
• Tender Type and Transaction Type 
• Clerk ID 
• Voucher Number 
• Transaction amounts 
• Balances 
• Approved messages 
• Declined messages 
• Approved HIP transaction data 
No signature line is required when printing an EBT receipt.  Optionally, a SIGNATURE NOT 
REQUIRED message can be printed. 
10.5.4.1 Tender Type and Transaction Type 
The receipt must print whether the transaction is a Food Stamp transaction or a Cash Benefit 
transaction.  It must also indicate the type of transaction attempted. 
Examples. Food Stamp Purchase 
 Cash Benefit Purchase with Cash Back 
10.5.4.2 Clerk ID 
Note: The Clerk ID is an optional receipt requirement. 
As an option, it may be retrieved from the transaction prompting sequence or a log on/log off 
function and printed on the receipt. 
Also, as an option, the device may prompt for a Clerk ID, whether it is on a transaction basis or 
within a log on/log off function.  The Clerk ID may be sent within the transaction’s message 
request and may be printed on the receipt.   
10.5.4.3 Voucher Number 
For Food Stamp Electronic Voucher transactions only, the manually entered Voucher Number 
must appear on the receipt. 
10.5.4.4 Transaction Amounts 
The food stamp dollar amount must be printed on a Food Stamp transaction receipt. 
The cash benefit dollar amount(s) must be printed on a Cash Benefit transaction receipt.  
It/They must be broken down for purchases versus cash back and include a total for both—if 
both amounts were entered. 
10.5.4.5 Balances 
For both Food Stamp transactions and Cash Benefit transactions, the ending balance must be 
printed on the receipt. 
As an option, the beginning EBT balance may be printed on the receipt by calculating the 
balance based on the ending balance and the amount of the transaction. 
EBT authorizers may return either a food stamp balance only, a cash benefit balance only, or 
both balances.  If a particular balance is not returned, do not print a balance of zero; omit the 
--- PAGE 114 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-37 
particular balance line altogether.  Balances of zero dollars should only be printed when zero is 
actually returned as the balance from the authorizer. 
10.5.4.6 Approved Transactions 
The Approval Number and message from the transaction response must be printed on the 
receipts for all "approved" EBT transactions. 
In the case when a PIN is entered, a PIN USED message prints on the transaction receipt. 
10.5.4.7 Declined Transactions 
All "declined" transactions must print a receipt.  The reason for the decline must be indicated on 
the receipt.  Transactions can be declined for the following reasons: 
• Insufficient funds 
• Bad PIN 
In the case of a decline due to "insufficient funds," the ending balance is returned and must be 
printed on the declined transaction receipt. 
In the case of a decline due to a "bad PIN," a declined transaction receipt must be printed.  The 
device may not prompt for reentry of the PIN without printing a receipt and retrying the 
transaction. 
10.5.4.8 Approved HIP transaction data 
The following fields must be printed on the receipt for the EBT FOOD approved HIP 
transactions: 
EBT HIP Transactions: 
• Incentive Eligible Amount 
• Incentive Earned or Incentive Returned 
• Month to date Incentive Earned 
 
Note: Incentive Earned is applicable to Sale transactions. Incentive Returned is applicable to 
Return transactions.

10.5.5 eWIC Transaction Processing 
This section discusses the following processing requirements for implementing the EBT version 
of Women, Infants and Children Nutrition Program solution (eWIC) for transaction processing 
involving BUYPASS: 
• eWIC Transaction Types 
• eWIC Prompt Codes 
• eWIC Payment Type 
• eWIC Authorizer 
• eWIC Totals 
• eWIC Product Data 
• eWIC Receipt Requirements 
10.5.5.1 eWIC Transaction Types 
Note: These specifications do not support Return transactions. 
The following nonfinancial transaction types are supported for eWIC: 
• eWIC Authorization (a.k.a. Benefits Inquiry) 
This transaction enables an eWIC client to query the eWIC host for the following information: 
 eWIC client list of eWIC-approved products 
 eWIC client account balance information 
This transaction is initiated by swiping an existing eWIC card at a POS device (device).  
When prompted, the eWIC client keys the necessary PIN into the device, and the device 
sends the eWIC Authorization Request to BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes the Request, 
and forwards the eWIC Authorization Response to the device. 
• eWIC Authorization (a.k.a. Benefits Inquiry) Cancellation 
This transaction cancels a previously submitted Authorization. 
Note: If there is a time-out or the eWIC client cancels the order, an eWIC Authorization 
Cancellation transaction is required. 
This transaction is initiated by swiping an existing eWIC card at a POS device (device).  
When prompted, the eWIC client keys the necessary PIN into the device, and the device 
sends the eWIC Authorization Cancellation Request to BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes 
the Request, and forwards the eWIC Authorization Cancellation Response to the device.  
The device displays/prints the eWIC account balance information from the Response. 
• eWIC Balance Inquiry 
This transaction enables an eWIC client to query the eWIC host for remaining eWIC account 
balance information. 
This transaction is initiated by swiping an existing eWIC card at a POS device (device).  
When prompted, the eWIC client keys the necessary PIN into the device, and the device 
sends the eWIC Balance Inquiry Request to BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes the Request, 
and forwards the eWIC Balance Inquiry Response to the device.  The device displays/prints 
the eWIC account balance information from the Response.

 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-39 
The following nonfinancial transaction types are supported for eWIC: 
• eWIC Purchase Completion 
This transaction performs an eWIC client’s purchase. 
Note: If there is a time-out or the eWIC client cancels the order, an eWIC Authorization 
Cancellation transaction is required. 
This transaction is initiated by swiping an existing eWIC card at a POS device (device).  
When prompted, the eWIC client keys the necessary PIN into the device, and the device 
sends the eWIC Authorization Request to BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes the Request, 
and forwards the eWIC Authorization Response to the device.  The device displays/prints 
the eWIC account balance information from the Response.  The clerk scans the items and 
enters any applicable manufacturer/cents-off discount coupon amount(s).  The device sends 
the eWIC Purchase Completion Request to BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes the Request, 
and sends the eWIC Purchase Completion Response to the device.  The device receives 
the Response. 
• eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void 
This transaction guarantees reversal/void of the effects of an eWIC Purchase Request at the 
eWIC host when an eWIC Purchase Response is not received or is received “late” (a time-
out or a late response) at the POS device (device). 
Notes: This transaction must be completed (The eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Response 
must be received by the device.) before any additional eWIC transactions can be 
sent from the device that originated the eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Request. 
If the eWIC host responds to the Purchase Reversal/Void Request, the Purchase 
Reversal/Void transaction is considered “processed” regardless of the Response 
Code. 
If no Purchase Reversal/Void Response is received, the Merchant must repeat the 
process at its earliest opportunity until a Purchase Reversal/Void Response to the 
eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Request is received. 
This transaction is initiated by the clerk determining that one of the following situations has 
occurred: 
 An eWIC Purchase Response has been received late; or 
 A time-out situation exists. 
The clerk sends the eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Request from the device to BUYPASS.  
BUYPASS processes the Request, and sends the eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Response 
to the device.  The device displays/prints the eWIC account balance information from the 
Response.

 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-40 
• eWIC Voucher Clear 
Note: This transaction is an optional transaction. 
This transaction allows the settlement of a previously authorized eWIC Voucher by 
electronically submitting—within established Merchant time limits—eWIC approvals received 
over the phone during a device/BUYPASS/eWIC host outage. 
This transaction is initiated by the clerk determining that the device/BUYPASS/eWIC host is 
offline.  The eWIC client’s purchase (including manufacturer discount(s)/cents-off coupons) 
is called in to the authorization center (center).  The center notifies the clerk whether the 
purchase is approved/declined. 
If the center declines the transaction, the eWIC client leaves. 
If the center approves the transaction, the center gives the clerk an eWIC Approval Number, 
and the clerk issues a paper eWIC Voucher to the eWIC client.  The eWIC Voucher contains 
the following information: 
 eWIC Voucher Number 
 eWIC Account Number 
 eWIC Approval Number 
 eWIC Transaction Amount 
Note: This information must be electronically submitted to the eWIC host within the 
Merchant’s specified time limit in order for the Merchant to receive payment. 
Using the information on the Merchant’s copy of the eWIC Voucher, the clerk keys the 
above information into the device together with any applicable manufacturer/cents-off 
discount coupon amount(s).  The device sends the eWIC Voucher Clear Request to 
BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes the Request, and sends an eWIC Voucher Clear 
Response to the device.  The device displays/prints the eWIC information from the eWIC 
Voucher Clear Response.

10.5.6 Healthy Incentives Program (HIP) Transaction 
Processing 
This section provides information about support for the Healthy Incentives Program (HIP) to 
evaluate health and nutrition promotion in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program 
(SNAP). 
Electronic benefit card programs from some US states are offering HIP in order to award 
bonuses for healthy food purchases.  The goal is to provide an incentive to purchase a target 
group of healthy foods. 
The incentive for each purchase is calculated by the authorizer.  Running totals are maintained 
by the authorizer. 
Additional balances are returned providing the incentive earned for the transaction and month-
to-date incentive earned.  The balances are reset at the beginning of the fiscal month. 
A new data element (No. 164 [EBT Program Data]) supports this feature.  For a complete 
description of this element, please see section 13.2, “Data Elements in Data Element Number 
Order.”  Data layout examples for this data element are contained in appendix M, “Element 
Format Examples for EBT Program Data.” 
This new data element is used in the EBT Data Segment (Data Segment No. 103).  For a 
complete description of this addition, please see section 12.4, “EBT Data Segment.” 
The receipt requirements listed in section 10.1.7, "Receipt Requirements,” also apply to HIP 
receipts. 
Please contact your Buypass representative for a list of states that support HIP.
