10.7 Stored Value Card Processing Requirements 
This section discusses the following stored value card (SVC) processing requirements: 
• Process overview 
• Card requirements 
• Supported transaction types 
• Receipt Requirements 
• Postal Code Capture 
• Track Support Requirements 
10.7.1 Process Overview 
A stored value card cannot be used for transactions until it has been activated.  There are three 
activation methods: 
• Activation without using a device 
• Activation using a device (predefined monetary limit) 
• Activation using a device (customer-defined monetary limit; issuer-activated) 
Under the first method, a stored value card is activated before a customer purchases it.  The 
card is ready to use immediately.  This method requires receipt by the vendor of a fulfillment 
letter confirming the cards' shipment to the client. 
Under the second method, a customer purchases a sealed SVC package that has a predefined 
monetary limit displayed on the cover.  The card is activated by swiping the package through 
the card reader of an indoor device.  If the card's magnetic stripe is invalid, the entire package is 
discarded, and the process is repeated with a new package.  If an "approved" Response is 
received, the card is active and ready to use—up to the predefined monetary limit. 
Under the third method, a customer purchases a stored value card that has no predefined 
value.  The card is activated by swiping it through a card reader and entering the activation 
amount at an indoor device.  If an “approved” Response is received, the card is active and 
ready to use—up to the defined monetary limit. 
The card can be used until its monetary limit is exhausted.  Clients can determine whether 
purchases can be made under a specific amount (i.e. $1.00). 
If an activated card is not used within the time frame established by its authorizer, it can be 
deactivated at any of the participating client’s devices. 
--- PAGE 123 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-46 
10.7.2 Card Requirements 
This section discusses the following card requirements for SVC processing: 
• Expiration date 
• Manual entry 
• Amount 
• Partial Approval 
• Embossing standards—First Data™ Premium Gift Card 
10.7.2.1 Expiration Date 
The device does not perform expiration date validation in a stored value card transaction. 
10.7.2.2 Manual Entry/Bar Code 
Manual entry may be allowed on a stored value card transaction.  It is dependent on the 
authorizer. 
If the POS device is unable to read the card's magnetic stripe, it should prompt the user to 
swipe the card again—up to three times. 
When manual entry is allowed, and the POS device is unable to read the magnetic stripe after 
three attempts, the POS device should prompt for manual entry of the Account Number and 
Expiration Date (Manual entry format:  MMYY).  The value to be used as the expiration date 
appears as an embossed 4-digit number on the First Data™ Standard Gift Card and the Stored 
Value Systems card.  An expiration date is not embossed on the front of the First Data™ 
Premium Gift Card; therefore, a default value of 1249 (Manual entry format:  MMYY) is sent by 
the POS device.  (Note:  The First Data™ Premium Gift Card has a 16-digit Account Number.) 
When manual entry is not allowed, and the POS device is unable to read the magnetic stripe 
after three attempts, a message should be displayed to the clerk, and the transaction ended. 
If manual entry is used, this fact is indicated on the receipt and journal by an asterisk (*). 
Bar Code Scanned Gift card should be treated as a manually entered transaction. It should be 
send like a manual transaction with Account Number and Expiration Date in the designated 
fields. The entry mode should be “01”. 
Blackhawk Gift card transactions should be treated as swiped transactions. The entry mode 
should be received as “90” for Blackhawk Scanned transactions. 
10.7.2.3 Amount 
When an activation (Please see section 10.7.3.6, “Activation Transaction.”) transaction, 
deactivation (Please see section 10.7.3.7, “Deactivation (Cash Out) Transaction.”) transaction, 
or a recharged/issued (Please see section 10.7.3.8, “Recharge/Issue Card Transaction.”) 
transaction is performed, a prompt for the activated/recharged/issued amount is required. 
10.7.2.4 Partial Approval 
Stored value card issuers have the ability to approve a transaction request for an amount that is 
different from the request amount.  When this occurs, the device will process the transaction for 
the approved amount returned in the transaction response and handle the remaining balance of 
the sale as a split tender transaction. 
When a transaction is partially approved by the issuer, transaction responses contain the 
following information: 
• A Response Code (Element No. 83) value of F (Indicates “approval, partial amount 
approved.”) 
--- PAGE 124 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-47 
• Approved Amount (Element No. 6) contains the approved partial amount, and the POS 
device must prompt for payment of the remaining balance due on the sale. 
• Approval Number (Element No. 5) contains the card balance—if returned by the issuer. 
 
When the transaction is processed as a split tender transaction the device will print a 
transaction receipt indicating the amount due on the transaction, display the amount due and 
offer options to complete the remaining balance of the sale.  Other options for payment include 
credit, debit, EBT, cash, or cancellation of the transaction.

10.7.3 Supported Transaction Types 
The following point-of-sale transactions are supported for SVC processing: 
• Purchase/Capture 
• Purchase Reversal 
• Authorization Only 
• Authorization Only Reversal 
• Merchandise Return 
• Activation 
• Deactivation 
• Recharge/Issue Card 
• Balance Merge 
• Replace Card 
• Balance Inquiry 
• Cancellation 
• Cancellation (Time-out Reversal) 
The following customer-activated transactions are supported for SVC processing: 
• Purchase/Capture 
• Authorization Only 
• Authorization Only Reversal 
• Cancellation (Time-out Reversal) 
The following additional transaction types are supported for InComm: 
• Account Verification (Preauthorization Activation) 
10.7.3.1 Purchase/Capture Transaction 
If an approved response is received, the card issuer deducts the purchase amount from the 
card's balance; otherwise, a declined response is sent to the device. 
10.7.3.2 Purchase Reversal Transaction 
This transaction adds the transaction amount to the card's balance.  This amount must be the 
exact amount of a previous SVC transaction.  (The previous transaction must have been done 
in the same business day.)  The POS device must subtract this amount from the SVC bucket 
and subtract this transaction from the SVC quantity. 
10.7.3.3 Authorization Only Transaction 
This transaction places a lock on the card.  The client decides the duration of the lock.  The 
Authorization Only Response contains the card's balance and the authorization number. 
10.7.3.4 Authorization Only Reversal Transaction 
This transaction is used if the device fails, or a communication problem occurs after the device 
receives an approved Authorization Only Response.  This transaction has an amount previously 
set by the client.  When this transaction is received, the card issuer unlocks the SVC account. 
10.7.3.5 Merchandise Return Transaction 
This transaction adds the given amount to the card's balance.  The POS device must subtract 
this amount from the SVC bucket and add this transaction to the SVC quantity. 
--- PAGE 127 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-50 
10.7.3.6 Activation Transaction 
This transaction activates the SVC's Account Number for a specific dollar amount on the card 
issuer's system.  After a successful Activation Transaction, charges can be made against this 
SVC account. 
10.7.3.7 Deactivation (Cash Out) Transaction 
For non-First Data™ Standard Gift Card transactions, this transaction is called a Deactivation 
transaction.  The deactivation amount in the transaction request must match the account 
balance.  Depending upon the client’s configuration, after a successful Deactivation transaction, 
the stored value card’s Account Number can be closed on the card issuer’s system, and 
charges can no longer be made against this Account Number. 
For First Data™ Premium Gift Card transactions, this transaction is called a Cash Out 
transaction.  The cash out amount in the transaction request must be greater than $0.00 and 
equal to or less than the account balance.  After the request is received, the account’s balance 
is taken to $0.00, and the amount used to bring the balance to $0.00 is returned to the POS 
device in the transaction response’s Approved Amount field.  Depending upon the client’s 
configuration, after a successful Cash Out transaction, the stored value card’s Account Number 
can remain open on the card issuer’s system with an account balance of $0.00.  (Note:  The 
First Data™ Premium Gift Card has a 16-digit Account Number.) 
The POS device must add this count to the SV1 count total. 
The POS device must subtract this amount from the SV1 amount total. 
10.7.3.8 Recharge/Issue Card Transaction 
This transaction adds the amount entered at the device to the card's current balance.  The 
added amount cannot cause the balance to be greater than the original value of the card. 
10.7.3.9 Balance Merge Transaction 
This transaction enables a customer to combine the balances of two stored value cards in 
his/her possession, and place that merged balance on one of those cards.  The account 
balance for the remaining card is reduced to $0.00. 
Note: The maximum number of cards that can be involved in this transaction is two.  If a 
customer has more than two stored value cards in his/her possession for which balances 
need to be merged, the transaction can be repeated until all balances have been 
merged to a single card, and the remaining card balances are reduced to $0.00. 
10.7.3.10 Replace Card Transaction 
This transaction enables a customer to transfer the balance of any lost, stolen, or damaged card 
to a new card with a completely new account number.  Receipts may be used to obtain the 
account number for lost or stolen cards.  This transaction replaces the lost, stolen, or damaged 
card.  The balance on the account for the lost, stolen, or damaged card is reduced to $0.00. 
10.7.3.11 Balance Inquiry Transaction 
This transaction is an information only transaction.  It provides the SVC's remaining balance.  
This transaction should not change the SVC quantity or amount totals. 
  
--- PAGE 128 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-51 
10.7.3.12 Cancellation Transaction 
This transaction is used to reverse any previous stored value gift card transaction.  The 
transaction amount must be the same amount as the transaction that is being reversed.  When 
this transaction is received, the card issuer unlocks the stored value card account. 
The POS device must subtract this count from the corresponding count total impacted by the 
original transaction. 
The POS device must subtract this amount from the corresponding amount total impacted by 
the original transaction. 
10.7.3.13 Cancellation (Time-out Reversal) Transaction 
This transaction is used if the device fails, or a communication problem occurs during a 
transaction.  The transaction has an amount previously set by the client.  When this transaction 
is received, the card issuer unlocks the SVC account. 
10.7.3.14 Account Verification (Preauthorization Activation) Transaction 
This transaction is used to verify that the POS, about to load/preload, is valid and ready to 
accept funds prior to accepting tender for the card.  
After performing the account verification, the POS may proceed with accepting tender and the 
activation. The subsequent activation is not associated with the original account verification.  
Note: This transaction type is only supported for InComm cards. 
10.7.4 Receipt Requirements 
The credit card receipt requirements listed in section 10.1.7, "Receipt Requirements," also apply 
to stored value card receipts. 
In addition to those requirements, the recharge amount prints on all approved stored value card 
receipts. 
In addition to those requirements, the remaining balance (positive/negative) prints on all 
approved and declined stored value card receipts.  The remaining balance (positive/negative) is 
returned as the Approval Number in the Authorization Response. 
No signature line is required when printing a stored value card receipt.  Optionally, a 
SIGNATURE NOT REQUIRED message can be printed. 
In cases where the PAN is printed on transaction receipts, it must be truncated to its last four 
digits.  A series of X’s equal to the number of truncated digits precedes these four digits for a 
field length equal to the original Account Number’s length.  Truncation of the Account Number is 
required on all customer-activated transactions.  The full Account Number should be retrievable 
from the POS device journal or transaction log for retrieval requests. 
Note: The last four digits of the 16-digit Account Number are truncated on First Data™ 
Premium Gift Card receipts only.  In this case, these last four digits are replaced by a 
series of four X’s. 
In the case of either a Balance Merge transaction or a Replacement/Balance Transfer 
transaction, it is preferred that the receipt contain the Account Number for the card with the final 
balance. 
10.7.5 Postal Code Capture 
Support has been added to allow a device to capture and send a customer’s ZIP Code™ in a 
closed loop prepaid card transaction.

 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications

August 07, 2026 
10-52 
The device sends a transaction request to BUYPASS containing the ZIP Code™ in Table ID 
003 of Element No. 111 (Variable Information Indicator).  (Please refer to chapter 13, “Data 
Element Descriptions,” for additional information about this data element.) 
The value of the ZIP Code™ is not validated by the issuer and does not have any bearing on 
the approval or decline of a transaction.  The ZIP Code™ is used for reporting purposes only. 
 
10.7.6 Track Support Requirements 
The following track support requirements must be met when processing all electronic stored 
value card transactions: 
• The default track that is sent to BUYPASS on an original transaction should be Track 2. 
• Card data provided in a Stored Value System (SVS) follow-on transaction can be either full 
or partial Track 2 Data. 
• Card data provided in a First Data™ Premium Gift Card (BIN 601056) follow-on transaction 
using either the token from the response or 601056* card number may be sent to BUYPASS 
as key entered transaction. 
• Card data provided in all other First Data™ Premium Gift Card follow-on transactions must 
be full Track 2 Data. 
Note: Partial Track 2 Data consists of the Primary Account Number, followed by “=” sign—
rather than a field separator—followed by the 4-digit expiration date (Storage format:  YYMM).  
No other discretionary data follows the 4-digit expiration date.

10.9 Loyalty Card Processing Requirements 
Loyalty card programs provide merchants with a system that allows consumers to accumulate 
real-time rewards, discounts, and messaging based on POS transactions.   
This section discusses the following loyalty card processing requirements: 
• Card requirements 
• Supported transaction types 
• Supported loyalty advice functions 
• Receipt requirements 
10.9.1 Card Requirements 
This section discusses the following card requirements for loyalty card processing: 
• Expiration date 
• Manual entry 
10.9.1.1 Expiration Date 
The device does not perform expiration date validation in a loyalty card transaction. 
10.9.1.2 Manual Entry 
Manual entry is allowed on a loyalty card transaction.  If the device is unable to read the card’s 
magnetic strip, it should prompt the user to swipe the card again—up to three times.  If unable 
to read the magnetic strip after three attempts, the device should prompt for manual entry of the 
Account Number and Expiration Date (MMYY).  The user is allowed to skip through the 
Expiration Date prompt when manually keyed data is entered and an expiration date is not 
present on the card.  When no expiration data is present, the device sends a default value of 
1249 (MMYY). 
Note: When a loyalty card is not present, the Street Address and Loyalty Phone Number 
associated with the consumer’s existing loyalty account are manually keyed at the 
device in lieu of the Loyalty Account Number. 
10.9.2 Supported Transaction Types 
The following point-of-sale transactions can include loyalty card information: 
• Purchase/Capture 
• Purchase Reversal 
• Time-out Reversal (TOR)

10.9.3 Supported Loyalty Advice Functions 
The following loyalty advice functions are supported for loyalty card processing: 
• Add account 
This transaction is used to add a new loyalty account to the loyalty host from a POS device.  
The clerk swipes a new loyalty card and enters the customer’s street number and telephone 
number. 
• Coupon redemption 
This transaction is used to redeem coupons for payment from a POS device.  The clerk 
swipes the loyalty card or manually keys the loyalty account number and enters the Coupon 
ID and Coupon Amount to redeem for payment.  If the loyalty card is not available, in lieu of 
the Loyalty Account Number, the clerk enters both the consumer’s street number and 
telephone number. 
• Expiration date update 
This transaction is used to update the expiration date of an account on the loyalty host from 
a POS device.  The clerk swipes the loyalty card or manually keys the account number.  If 
the loyalty card is not available, in lieu of the Loyalty Account Number, the clerk enters both 
the consumer’s street number and telephone number.  The host will then extend the loyalty 
account for a predefined amount of time. 
• Account inquiry 
This transaction is used to inquire about the status of a loyalty account from a POS device.  
The clerk swipes the loyalty card or manually keys the account number.  If the loyalty card is 
not available, in lieu of the Loyalty Account Number, the clerk enters both the consumer’s 
street number and telephone number.  The host returns the Loyalty Print Data in the 
response.  The data returned to the device is a pre-programmed message maintained by 
the merchant at the loyalty host. 
• Points redemption 
This transaction is used to redeem points for payment from a POS device.  The clerk swipes 
the loyalty card or manually keys the Loyalty Account Number and enters the number of 
points to redeem for payment.  If the loyalty card is not available, in lieu of the Loyalty 
Account Number, the clerk enters both the consumer’s street number and telephone 
number. 
• Reversal of coupon redeem 
This transaction is used to reverse coupons redeemed on a previously approved coupon 
redemption transaction from a POS device.  The clerk swipes the loyalty card or manually 
keys the account number, and enters the Coupon ID, Coupon Amount, and approval 
number of the previous transaction receipt.  If the loyalty card is not available, in lieu of the 
Loyalty Account Number, the clerk enters both the consumer’s street number and telephone 
number. 
• Reversal of points redeemed 
This transaction is used to reverse points redeemed on a previously approved point 
redemption transaction from a POS device.  The clerk swipes the loyalty card or manually 
keys the account number, and enters the point amount and approval number of the previous 
transaction receipt.  If the loyalty card is not available, in lieu of the Loyalty Account Number, 
the clerk enters both the consumer’s street number and telephone number. 
• Sale update 
--- PAGE 135 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-58 
This transaction is used to update the loyalty host with noncredit card sale data for a loyalty 
account from a POS device.  The clerk swipes the loyalty card or manually keys the Loyalty 
Account Number, and enters the amount of the noncredit card or cash sale.  If the loyalty 
card is not available, in lieu of the Loyalty Account Number, the clerk enters both the 
consumer’s street number and telephone number. 
• Account update 
This transaction is used to update street address and phone number information on a loyalty 
account from a POS device.  The clerk swipes the loyalty card and must enter both the new 
street number and new telephone number the customer wants to associate with the existing 
loyalty account. 
• Totals Report, Loyalty 
This transaction is used to request a summary of all loyalty transactions and subtotal by card 
number.  The clerk selects the totals menu option from the loyalty menu at the device, which 
initiates a request to the loyalty host.  The host returns the loyalty totals report to the device 
to print.

to loyalty cards. 
Additional loyalty card information that can be included on loyalty card receipts is described in 
Appendix K.  Additional Information Data Layouts, in Table 008, “Loyalty Information – Version 
1,” and Table 010, “Loyalty Information – Version 2.”  Any of this information that is received by 
the device is printed.

10.10  Software Update Processing Requirements 
Note: Vendors who support their own applications do not use software update processing. 
Software update processing involves an automated request by an active device for a full 
application download to the device from the device management system supported by 
BUYPASS. 
The following steps must be included in this process: 
1. A bit is set on the merchant profile at BUYPASS indicating that the device must request a 
DLL. 
2. BUYPASS sends a Download Indicator of 1 in the response to the next transaction request 
from the device. 
3. The device sends a Table Load request to BUYPASS. 
4. BUYPASS responds to the Table Load request by sending the Software Dial Load Data 
Segment and Software IP Load Data Segment. 
5. The device stores the data received in the Software Load response: 
a. New Software Version 
b. Software Terminal Record ID 
c. Software Load Phone Number or Software Load IP/URL Address 
d. Software Load Request Date 
e. Software Load Request Time 
6. At the designated date and time, the device dials the Software Load Phone Number 
/Software Load IP/URL Address and initiates a request for a full application load. 
7. Upon completion of the full application load, the device dials BUYPASS and requests a 
Table Load. 
8. BUYPASS responds by sending the Table Load without requiring the bit to be set on the 
merchant profile. 
Notes: The device can attempt to request the automated full application load a maximum of 
three times. 
 If a load request to Software Load Phone Number/Software Load IP/URL Address is 
unsuccessful, the device prints the “decline” message.

10.11 Electronic Mail Processing 
This chapter contains information about electronic mail processing involving a client, BUYPASS, 
and a client’s store point-of-sale (POS) device. 
10.11.1 Electronic Mail Retrieval 
Data originating from a client can be sent to the client’s store POS device via BUYPASS.  The 
data is sent to BUYPASS where it is stored until transmission to the client’s store POS device in 
one of the following ways: 
• A device operator, using the client’s store POS device, sends an Electronic Mail Request for 
the file to BUYPASS; or 
• BUYPASS responds to an automated Electronic Mail Request from the client’s store POS 
device. 
Either of these methods can be used prior to the end-of-business day, up to the time when a 
device ends its day. 
The Electronic Mail Request in either case uses a Prompt Code of 981. 
Note: For retrieval of proprietary card data, the Electronic Mail Request uses a Prompt Code of 
996. 
There can be up to 750 bytes of print data for each Electronic Mail Request. 
10.11.2 Electronic Mail Submission 
In addition, a client’s store POS device can send data to the client via BUYPASS in one of the 
following ways: 
• A device operator, using the client’s store POS device, sends data to BUYPASS using an 
Electronic Mail Request; or 
• The client’s store POS device sends data to BUYPASS using an automated Electronic Mail 
Request. 
The Electronic Mail Request uses a Prompt Code of 995. 
The Electronic Mail Request contains up to 217 bytes of data. 
BUYPASS sends an Electronic Mail Response to the client’s store POS device to confirm 
receipt of the Electronic Mail Request. 
The data is stored at BUYPASS.

10.13 Payment Tokenization 
Note: Please check with your First Data Certification Representative for the availability of this 
new feature. 
This chapter provides an overview and describes processing requirements for implementing the 
Payment Token processing feature involving the BUYPASS platform ATL105 message formats 
(software version ATL105). 
With the introduction of new payments, such as, mobile phones, and tablets, etc., the need for 
advanced protection against counterfeit, account misuse, and other forms of fraud, has 
increased. 
Visa, MasterCard, American Express, Interlink, and Maestro have introduced payment token 
which is the replacement of the Primary Account Number (PAN) with a token number that 
represents the PAN by device and/or e-commerce payment transactions.  
Payment token issuance is performed by a token vault that generates and stores the payment 
token and the associated cardholder PAN. The operator of the token vault is referred to as the 
token service provider. The token requestor is typically an acquirer, merchant or digital wallet 
provider that will use the payment token to replace the PAN in its database and in transaction 
processing. Payment processes that need to support token processing may include 
authorization, capture, clearing, and exception processing. 
Note: For additional information on payment tokenization terminologies, please refer to 
Appendix O (Payment Tokenization Terminologies) in this document. 
  
--- PAGE 140 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-63 
 
10.13.1 Salient Features of Payment Tokenization 
Following are the general features of Tokenization: 
• Payment Token ranges will be in the existing ranges of the relevant card brand 
• Payment Tokenization is the replacement of the Primary Account Number (PAN) with a 
token number that represents the PAN by device and/or eCommerce payment transactions 
• Payment Tokens are mapped to the PAN, leveraging the existing payments infrastructure 
and messaging formats for authorization and processing 
• The Payment Token will be used for the entire life-cycle of the transaction for all card brands 
• EMVCo manages the Payment Token Standard 
 
10.13.2 Payment Tokenization Usages 
A Payment token transaction, where the actual card primary account number is replaced by an 
association payment token, could take place in any of the following scenarios: 
• NFC transactions, when customer's NFC device is sending Payment Token instead of actual 
card number 
• eCommerce transactions with security data that contains token cryptogram, like VPAS, 
UCAF 
• Card-on-file transactions, where the initial transaction contains the token with valid 
cryptogram. The token and token related data could be saved by merchants, and used for 
subsequent transactions, like recurring payment 
The following sections describe the Payment Token transactions which are currently supported 
by BUYPASS: 
10.13.2.1 Near Frequency Communication (NFC) - In Person Purchase 
Consumer has a device such as tablet, smartphone, etc. and the device has been provisioned 
with payment capability. A token is provisioned in the consumer’s device. The consumer walks 
to a store, for example, Coffee Is Us and buys a double espresso. He uses his “digital wallet” 
instead of the Coffee Is Us Merchant App on his smartphone/tablet to tap and pay. The 
tokenized card information is read and the appropriate contactless data is captured by the POS. 
Merchant submits the authorization as a contactless transaction exactly as they do today. 
10.13.2.2 Mobile App (In App) – eCommerce 
Consumer has a device such as tablet, smartphone, etc. and the device has been provisioned 
with payment capability. A token is provisioned in the consumer’s device. Consumer activates 
the “digital wallet” on the device when using a Merchant App for purchasing. For example: the 
consumer downloads the “TV Store” app (an example of Merchant App) to his/her device. The 
consumer then decides to buy a TV and uses the TV Store app instead of going to TVStore.com 
website or to the physical store location to initiate the transaction. The TV Store App asks if the 
consumer wants to pay with the “digital wallet”. The Merchant App interacts with the wallet to 
get the token and merchant sends authorization request with appropriate data including the 
cryptogram. 
--- PAGE 141 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-64 
10.13.2.3 Mobile App (In App) – eCommerce Subsequent Transactions 
(such as Recurring, etc) 
Consumer purchases 4 pairs of shoes on Fancyshoe.com via the Merchant App on their 
tablet/smartphone and decides to pay with the “digital wallet” on the tablet/smartphone. The 
merchant realizes that they have only 3 pairs in stock and 1 pair is on back order. Depending on 
the timeframe, the card brand allows the authorization to remain valid, while a new authorization 
may be required once the 4th pair of shoe is shipped. If a new authorization is required, there 
are specific field requirements that must be included in the authorization request for a token 
transaction to ensure that the subsequent authorization is not declined. Specific field 
requirements vary by card brand. 
 
10.13.2.4 Card On File (COF) 
Consumer has established a relationship with an eCommerce merchant, where they select the 
option of storing their cardholder data (card number, expiration date) with the merchant for 
future transactions. In this scenario the payment token provided by the card brand replaces the 
PAN that is stored at the merchant’s end. 
 
10.13.2.4.1 Stored Credentials 
A stored credential is information, including, but not limited to, an account number or a payment 
token. It is stored by a merchant, its agent, a payment facilitator or a staged digital wallet 
operator to process future transactions for a cardholder. 
A credential is not considered a stored credential when details of a card are stored to: 
• Complete a single transaction 
• Complete multiple authorizations related to the initial transaction, such as Incremental 
transactions 
Types of Stored Credential transactions are as follows: 
• Cardholder-Initiated Transaction (CIT) – A cardholder-initiated transaction is any 
transaction where the cardholder is actively participating in the transaction. This can be 
either at a terminal in-store or through a checkout experience online, or a subsequent stored 
credential transaction. 
• Merchant-Initiated Transaction (MIT) – A merchant-initiated transaction is a subsequent 
transaction with already stored credentials. The cardholder has given prior consent to the 
merchant to store payment credentials for future use without active engagement from the 
cardholder. 
Subsequent Transaction with respect to Stored Credentials: 
Once the card credentials are shared for stored credential at a merchant location or website, the 
following transactions are considered to be subsequent transactions: 
Standing instructions MITs: 
• Separate transaction to buy a different item, once again, using the same card at the same 
merchant  location or website 
• Recurring transaction associated with the original transaction 
• Installment transaction associated with the original transaction

10.14 EMV Processing Requirements 
Note: For EMV processing -  
• Refer to First Data EMV Implementation Guide, available on the Direct Platform 
Specifications Portal. 
• The EMV Implementation Guide must be used in conjunction with the ATL105 Message 
Format Specifications. 
This section discusses the following EMV card processing requirements: 
• Process Overview 
• Card requirements 
• Supported transaction types 
• EMV PIN (Personal Identification Number) Processing 
 
10.14.1 Process Overview 
EMV stands for Europay, MasterCard and Visa. It represents a global standard for inter-
operation of integrated circuit cards (IC cards or "chip cards") through IC card capable point-of-
sale (POS) terminals and automated teller machines (ATMs). EMV is used for authenticating 
credit and debit card transactions. 
The most widely known chip card implementations of EMV standard are: 
• VSDC - VISA 
• M/Chip - MasterCard 
• AEIPS - American Express 
• J Smart - JCB 
• D-PAS - Discover/Diners Club International 
There are two types of chip card technology – contact and contactless: 
• Contact - When a chip card is inserted into a card acceptance device, the contact allows the 
chip to connect to a reader. This connection enables the chip to get power from and 
exchange data with the terminal. 
• Contactless – When a contactless chip card is held within a couple of inches of a 
contactless-capable reader, the reader energizes the chip embedded in the card and allows 
exchange of data via radio frequency without the card ever leaving the cardholder’s 
possession.  
The benefits of EMV contact and contactless payment cards include: 
• Improved security against credit card fraud through use of a unique online cryptogram 
• Enhanced cardholder verification methods 
• Chip stores more information than magnetic stripe cards 
• Possibility for finer control of "offline" credit card transaction approvals 
In order to perform offline data authentication, a terminal must be configured with the necessary 
card scheme public keys. 
The card scheme (MasterCard, Visa, and Amex) Certification Authority distributes the card 
scheme Certificate of Authority (CA) Public Key to acquirers (i.e. First Data). Acquirers are 
responsible for the distribution of the card scheme CA Public Key to all terminals that support 
offline data authentication. 
Common AID is another application that incorporates the EMV standard.  This application can 
exist on the issued card and the terminal that can be selected for performing a financial 
--- PAGE 157 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-80 
transaction.  There are four categories of Common AIDs. Any of these AIDs may be used in 
processing a Common AID transaction.  
• Visa Common AID 
• US Maestro AID 
• DNA Shared Debit AID  
• Discover Common AID  
The Common AID applications are actually implementations of VSDC (for Visa Common AID), 
M/Chip (for US Maestro AID) and D-PAS (for DNA Shared Debit AID and Discover Common 
AID).Those applications are licensed to other debit networks (like Star, NYCE, Pulse, etc.) and 
provide compliance with the Durbin amendment. 
DNA Shared Debit AID is used for ‘debit only’ cards that do not support MasterCard, Visa or 
Discover Signature Debit. 
Merchants should submit Visa and US Maestro Common AID transactions as ‘credit / 0100 / 
Dual message’ requests.  This will provide merchants with optimal routing options.  If First Data 
receives a credit transaction request with cashback with one of these Common AIDs, First Data 
will route this transaction, except Discover, to a ‘single message’ debit network. Discover 
already supports cashback on credit requests.  First Data does not support cashback for Visa or 
MasterCard credit / Signature Debit transactions. 
DNA Shared Debit AID is limited to the ‘debit / 0200 / single message’ networks.  As a result, 
merchants should submit DNA Shared Debit AID transactions as ‘debit/0200/single message’ 
requests. Cards supporting the DNA Shared Debit AID do not support Visa or MasterCard 
Signature Debit.  If First Data receives a debit transaction request with cashback with this 
Common AID, First Data will route this transaction to a ‘single message’ debit network. 
Note: Please check with your First Data Certification Representative for the availability of this 
new feature. 
 
10.14.2 Card Requirements 
This section discusses the following card requirements for EMV card processing: 
• Expiration Date 
• Manual Entry 
• Supported Cards 
• Supported Transaction Types 
• Receipt Requirements 
 
10.14.2.1 Expiration Date 
The device does not perform expiration date validation in an EMV card transaction. 
10.14.2.2 Manual Entry 
Manual entry of the EMV account number is allowed on all EMV card transactions.  If the 
account number is keyed, the device prompts for Expiration Date (Format:  MMYY) and any 
other optional or conditional data, such as card present, AVS, or CVV code. 
Note: If manual entry is used, this fact is indicated on the receipt and journal by an asterisk (*) 
before the account number. 
10.14.2.3 Supported Cards 
The following credit cards are supported for EMV processing: 
• American Express

• MasterCard®

10.14.2.4 Supported Transaction Types 
The following point-of-sale transactions are supported for EMV card processing: 
• Purchase 
• Purchase/Capture 
• Authorization Only 
• Merchandise Return 
• Purchase Reversal 
• Balance Inquiry 
• Cancellation 
• Time-out Reversal (TOR) 
Note: A Time-out Reversal (TOR) transaction is used to reverse a transaction, if the device 
fails, or the transaction is aborted after communication has been initiated to the host. 
 EMV data is not required on Reversal transactions. 
10.14.2.5 Receipt Requirements 
The credit card receipt requirements listed in section 10.1.7, “Receipt Requirements,” also apply 
to EMV cards. 
Two elements of the receipt (whether to print a signature line and what to display as a card 
type) are provided in the authorization response message for a Common AID transaction.  The 
disposition of the transaction is also provided indicating how the transaction was authorized – as 
a single message (debit) transaction or as a Dual message (credit) transaction. 
 
 
10.14.3 EMV PIN (Personal Identification Number) Processing 
Note: Please check with your First Data Certification Representative for the availability of these 
new features. 
--- PAGE 159 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-82 
MasterCard has mandated that Point-of-Sale devices that support EMV PIN must support both 
online PIN and offline PIN processing.  Visa also supports this functionality but does not 
mandate online PIN support. This means that POS Devices processing transactions that are 
initiated from chip cards for credit and signature debit must have the capability to submit a PIN 
in the authorization request message submitted. 
Following are the two modes of PIN validation during EMV payment card processing:  
• Online PIN: This is applicable for credit or debit transactions, in which the PIN is 
electronically sent to and validated by the card issuer. The potential PIN requirement for 
credit transactions where a PIN pad is present is new with EMV. 
• Offline PIN: Instead of sending the PIN to the issuer, the PIN entered by the consumer is 
matched to that on an application housed on the EMV chip card. This functionality is 
exclusive to EMV card transactions. The authorization request may still be sent to the issuer.  
Note: In a traditional PIN Debit transaction, the PIN field is mandatory. Either a PIN or all 
F’s, for offline PIN, must be sent in this mandatory field or the transaction will decline as 
“invalid transaction”. In a credit/signature debit transaction, a PIN of all F’s is NOT required 
since PINs are an optional field for a credit/signature debit transaction. 
 
10.14.4 EMV Fallback Transaction Processing 
For the purposes of this document, the term “Fallback” is defined as the acceptance of chip 
cards via magnetic-stripe processing at a chip-capable device.  EMV POS Solutions must 
accept both chip and magnetic-stripe cards and thus have both chip and magnetic-stripe 
readers. 
If a chip card is presented at a chip capable terminal and a chip transaction cannot be 
performed, then the merchant may process the chip card as a magnetic stripe read (swipe). The 
resultant transaction is referred to as a fallback transaction and must be properly identified as 
such in the authorization message. Fallback transactions are less secure than EMV but 
continue to protect the merchant from the liability shift when performed correctly. 
Regardless, a Fallback will occur whenever an EMV Certified solution cannot read or obtain a 
viable matching AID.  MSR/Fallback Entry Mode sample usage for contact transactions are as 
following: 
IF THEN STATUS 
• The device is EMV 
enabled and 
• The card is chip and 
• The card is swiped 
Always send the Fallback Entry 
Mode of ‘80’or spec equivalent 
EMV Fallback transaction 
• The card is NOT a chip 
card or 
• The device is not chip 
capable and 
• The card is swiped 
Send as a MSR Entry Mode of 
‘90’or spec equivalent 
 
Regular MSR swipe 
transaction

This chapter discusses the BUYPASS variable length message formats. 
Note: For detailed information about individual data elements within the messages, refer to 
chapter 13, “Data Element Descriptions.”  The element descriptions in this chapter focus 
on the purpose of the data, rather than a detailed description of the content of the data.

• Financial transactions 
• Loyalty card transactions 
• ECA/ TeleCheck® service transactions 
• Totals 
 Sending totals to BUYPASS 
 Sending totals with proprietary data to BUYPASS

 Retrieving electronic mail from BUYPASS  
 Sending electronic mail to BUYPASS  
• Communications test 
• Downloads 
 Table Load (Load Type:  P) 
 Phone Load (Load Type:  P) 
 Date and Time Load (Load Type:  D) 
 Software Load (Load Type:  P) 
A request is a message from a customer’s device. 
A response is a message from BUYPASS.

The following message format characteristics are used—where applicable—for each message: 
• Data Section Number 
Unique number (1–3) that identifies one of the three sections within a Financial 
Transaction/Totals Request message record. 
• Field Number 
Relative number that identifies the relative position, beginning with 1, of each data element 
within a message record. 
• Segment Number 
Unique number (100–105, 108–114, and DL1–DL5) that identifies one of the data segments 
within a message record. 
Note: Data Segment Nos. 106 and 107 are reserved for proprietary use. 
• Segment Name 
Unique name associated with a specific data segment within a message record.  Each 
segment contains a specific type of data. 
• Element Number 
Unique number associated with a data element.  Use this number to locate an element and 
its description in chapter 13, “Data Element Descriptions.” 
• Element Name 
Identifies a specific unit of information, regardless of where it appears in a message record. 
• Position 
Identifies the starting position for a data element within a message record, relative to 1. 
• Length 
Identifies the maximum or fixed number of characters a data segment or data element can 
contain. 
• Required/Optional/Conditional Entry 
R indicates a data element is required in the message; O indicates a data element is 
optional in the message; and C indicates a data element is conditional in the message. 
• Description 
Describes the purpose of the data element.  For additional information, refer to chapter 13, 
“Data Element Descriptions.”

11.7 Downloads 
This section contains message formats for the following downloads: 
• Table Load 
• Phone Load 
• Date and Time Load 
• Software Load 
Note: The Software Dial Load Data Segment and Software IP Load Data Segment are 
used only for devices loaded through the BUYPASS device management system. 
• TransArmor Key and Key ID Load 
• Proprietary Data Load 
The following items must be downloadable: 
• Dialing strings 
• BUYPASS Merchant Numbers 
• Card types 
• Cut times 
• Dates 
• Times 
• Passwords 
Note: The device application/system software should not be activated until at least one 
successful Table Load has been performed.  When the software is not activated, all 
BUYPASS transactions except downline loads should be prohibited at the device. 
Downloads must be capable of being requested by manual user intervention, such as selecting 
a function.  The device must also be capable of automatically requesting a download based on 
the host’s response to a device’s transaction request. 
In the case of dial communications, when indicated by the host’s response that a download is 
requested, the device receives an ENQ after acknowledging the host’s response, rather than an 
EOT.  The device should stay on-line and send up a Partial Load Request. 
Note: If the controller is capable of queuing multiple transactions, the load request should not 
be sent until the controller has cleared its queue of all transactions. 
The response is a Table Load or a subset of the complete table load containing only dial string 
information.  The information in the download is used in the very next transaction performed by 
the device. 
Please refer to section 11.1, “Financial Transactions,” for Financial Transaction message 
formats. 
Please refer to section 11.2, “Loyalty Card Transactions,” for Loyalty Card message formats. 
Please refer to section 11.3, “ECA/ TeleCheck® Service Transactions,” for ECA/ TeleCheck® 
service message formats. 
Please refer to section 11.4, “Totals,” for Totals message formats. 
Please refer to section 11.5, “Electronic Mail,” for Electronic Mail message formats. 
Please refer to section 11.6, “Communications Test,” for Communications Test message 
formats.

11.7.2 Phone Load 
This section contains request and response message formats for a phone load. 
This load provides the device with the dialing telephone number, redial count, access code, and 
pause indicator information needed to operate properly. 
The load flag in the merchant’s profile on BUYPASS must be set to PHON for this load to take 
place.  A BUYPASS representative can change this load flag, or it can be changed 
automatically following a full load.  If the load flag is not set, the Downline Load Response will 
consist only of an error message block and a terminating block.

11.7.6 Proprietary Data Load 
This section contains request and response message formats for a Proprietary Data Load. 
Proprietary Data Load is used to send Custom Receipt Text, support the Site Configuration, Fuel 
Volume, and Dynamic Card Table Data load, and allow the Host Discount processing. Data 
Element 83 (Response Code) which is returned on an End of Day Totals Response, indicates that 
the Proprietary Data is available for loading.  When indicated that this data is available, the POS 
device will format a Proprietary Data Load Request. 
Note: The Proprietary Data Load functions occur at end of day only as part of the Day Close 
processing. These functions are prompted as part of End of Day Totals Response and cannot be 
supported at any time of the day. 
Data Element 78 (Prompt Code) indicates the request/response and format of the Proprietary 
Data. For example the 901 Custom Receipt Text format will differ from the 902 Dynamic Card 
Table Load. 
11.7.6.1 Request 
Each Proprietary Data Load Request contains the following two data sections: 
• Data Section No. 1 
 Data Section No. 1 contains the following two data elements: 
 Message Format Version Identifier (Element No. 55) 
 Number of Segments (Element No. 63) 
Please refer to chapter 13, “Data Element Descriptions,” for additional information about these 
data elements. 
• Data Section No. 3 
 Data Section No. 3 contains the following data segment: 
 Proprietary Data Load Segment (Data Segment No. 118) 
 Please refer to chapter 12, “Data Segment Formats,” for additional information about this 
data segment. 
Note: Proprietary Data Load Request messages do not contain the Standard Data Message 
Data Segment (Data Segment 100). 
The following table illustrates the layout of a Proprietary Data Load Request message:

11.8 EMV Financial Transaction 
This section contains message formats for the EMV card transaction request and response. 
Please refer to section 11.1, “Financial Transactions,” for Financial Transaction message 
formats. 
11.8.1 Request 
Each Financial Transaction Request contains three data sections: 
• Data Section No. 1 
Data Section No. 1 contains the following two data elements that are the same for each 
Financial Transaction Request message: 
 Message Format Version Identifier (Element No. 55) 
 Number of Segments (Element No. 63) 
Please refer to chapter 13, “Data Element Descriptions,” for additional information about 
these data elements. 
• Data Section No. 2 
Data Section No. 2 contains the following data segment that is the same for each Financial 
Transaction Request message: 
 Standard Message Data Segment (Data Segment No. 100) 
Please refer to chapter 12, “Data Segment Formats,” for additional information about this 
data segment. 
• Data Section No. 3 
Data Section No. 3 contains one, or more of the data segments in Chapter 12. See the Data 
Section No. 3 table below for specifics on what segments may be included. 
 Fleet Data Segment (Data Segment No. 101) 
 Product Code Data Segment (Data Segment No. 102) 
 Purchase Card Data Segment (Data Segment No. 104) 
 Variable Information Data Segment (Data Segment No. 111) 
 EMV Request Data Segment (Data Segment No. 130) 
Please refer to chapter 12, “Data Segment Formats,” for additional information about these data 
segments. 
Note: The maximum length of a Financial Transaction Request Message is 4,000 bytes.

11.9 CA Public Key File Load 
This section contains request and response message formats for a CA Public Key File Load. 
11.9.1 Request 
Each Financial Transaction Request contains three data sections: 
• Data Section No. 1 
Data Section No. 1 contains the following two data elements that are the same for each 
Financial Transaction Request message: 
 Message Format Version Identifier (Element No. 55) 
 Number of Segments (Element No. 63) 
Please refer to chapter 13, “Data Element Descriptions,” for additional information about 
these data elements. 
• Data Section No. 2 
Data Section No. 2 contains the following data segment that is the same for each Financial 
Transaction Request message: 
 Standard Message Data Segment (Data Segment No. 100) 
• Data Section No. 3 
Data Section No. 3 contains none, one, or more of the following data segment(s) that is/are 
unique to the Financial Transaction Request message type. 
 Fleet Data Segment (Data Segment No. 101) 
 Product Code Data Segment (Data Segment No. 102) 
 Purchase Card Data Segment (Data Segment No. 104) 
 Variable Information Data Segment (Data Segment No. 111) 
 CA Public Key File Load Segment (Data Segment No. 132) 
Please refer to chapter 12, “Data Segment Formats,” for additional information about these data 
segments.

12.3 Product Code Data Segment 
This section describes Data Segment No. 102, Product Code Data Segment. 
Note:  This segment can be used for all card types except for Comdata cards. 
Note:  This segment is mutually exclusive with segment 157 Adjusted Product Code Data.  
Merchants should send one or the other but never both. If both the segments are sent, the 
transaction will be declined. 
When a Financial Transaction request includes the Product Code Data Segment, the products 
within this segment must meet the following requirements: 
• Fuel products must always be the first products in the segment. 
• For EV charging transactions, the EV fuel product code should be the first product code in 
the segment. 
• A maximum of ten products is allowed in the segment. 
• The total of product amounts in the segment must equal the total of the amounts [Element 
No. 41 (Fuel Purchase Amount), Element No. 58 (Nonfuel Amount), Element No. 99 (Tax 
Amount) and Element No. 17 (Cash Amount)] in the Standard Message Data Segment 
(Data Segment No. 100). 
• When tax product codes are included in the segment, the total dollar amount of tax products 
is also reported in Element No. 99 (Tax Amount) in the Standard Message Data Segment 
(Data Segment No. 100). 
• All fuel merchants must send fuel and nonfuel product data. 
Note: A unique Product Code must be sent for each type of fuel purchase. 
Note: With the growth of fleet industry and to fulfil the needs of the Over the Road Trucking 
(OTR) industry, BUYPASS can accept transactions with multiple fuels (e.g., purchase of Diesel, 
DEF, REEFER), all on 1 transaction. It is estimated that up to 30% of fuel transactions in OTR 
require fill-ups involving multiple Fuel Type Codes.  Now, fuel merchants can allow multiple fuel 
fill-ups in 1 transaction. With the support of multiple fuels, a merchant must send the Product 
segment to BUYPASS with all the fuel codes and any non-fuel codes with all the relevant 
information like quality, unit of measure, unit price, and product amount. Also, the merchant 
must ensure to send the primary fuel (fuel used for the primary fuel need of the truck/vehicle) as 
the very first product code within the Product segment. Refer to the Product Code Data segment 
for the details on the product information layout and rules. 
This data segment can appear in any of the fields in Data Section No. 3.  (Please refer to 
section 11.1, “Financial Transactions,” for additional information about Data Section No. 3.) 
It has a maximum length of 381 alphanumeric characters (001–381/a–z/A–Z). 
It originates at the device. 
The following table illustrates the layout of the Product Data Segment: 
Notes: A Field Separator always follows Segment Type and Segment Length.  A Field 
Separator follows Product Amount when Product Amount is the very last element in the 
segment.  When a field is not populated, still send the Field Separator. 
 A Product Data Field Delimiter always follows Quantity and Unit Price.  A Product Data 
Field Delimiter follows Product Amount when Product Amount is not the last element in 
the segment.  When a field is not populated, still send the Product Data Field Delimiter. 
 For an example of this segment, please refer to Appendix B.  POS Purchase Example. 
In the following table, the ▲ symbol represents a Field Separator, and the \ character is a

12.9 Check Data Segment 
This section describes Data Segment No. 110, Check Data Segment. 
This data segment can appear in any of the fields in Data Section No. 3.  (Please refer to 
section 11.1, “Financial Transactions,” for additional information about Data Section No. 3.) 
It has a maximum length of 168 alphanumeric characters (001–168/a–z/A–Z). 
It originates at the device. 
The following table illustrates the layout of the Check Data Segment: 
Note: All fields are separated by Field Separators.  When a field is not populated, still send the 
Field Separator. 
MICR readers provide the flexibility to format the MICR fields transmitted to the host for 
authorization. There are two types of MICR formats used in check services: 
 
1) Full MICR Line – TAC Format -  Example T999999999A999999999999999999C999999   
2) Full MICR Line - Format RAW TOAD  
 
TOAD is a symbol substitution of the MICR characters appearing on the check.  
 
Here, 
T replaces  
  This symbol is used to indicate the beginning and ending of the bank’s 9-digit 
routing transit number. 
O replaces  
  This symbol is used to indicate the ‘On-Us’ field usually grouped around the 
account number or check serial number. 
A replaces   
  This symbol is used to indicate the beginning and ending of the encoded dollar 
amount field. 
 D replaces  
  This symbol is a dash usually appearing in the account number field in the MICR 
line. 
 
 
 
 
 

--- PAGE 240 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
12-26 
 
 
TOAD Example: 
 
      
MICR reader output: T123456780T0301 123D456D7O 
 
‘BUY2’ and ‘ALB1’ are the two types of alphanumeric headers assigned by Certegy (Tele credit) 
Check Services to uniquely identify each customer.  Buypass has to support the check data 
segment for both the ‘BUY2’ and ‘ALB1’ formats. Therefore, a new field, Alternate MICR 
Indicator, is introduced to identify the ‘ALB1’ format so that Buypass can support both the RAW 
TOAD MICR and TAC MICR data.  
 
A merchant, who wants to support the Alternate MICR format, should send ‘Y’ in the new field 
Alternate MICR Indicator introduced in the 110-check data segment and typically use this field in 
a check transaction along with the MICR/Driver’s License number.  
 
The element ‘131’ is currently in use. Hence, the element number ‘239’ is used for Alternate 
MICR Indicator. 
 
Note: Merchants who want support for the RAW MICR format should send Alternate MICR 
Indicator.

12.16 Proprietary Data Load Segment 
This section describes Data Segment No. 118, Proprietary Data Load Segment. 
It is used to request Customer Specific Proprietary data for loading or Customer Specific 
Proprietary data for capturing at the BUYPASS FEP.  This function will be similar to Electronic

Host Discounts, and Site Configuration, and Fuel Volume.  Dynamic Card Table, and Custom 
Receipt Text, and Host Discounts are driven by the host in a data push to the POS, while Site

12.16.3 Proprietary Load Request Data, Prompt Code 903 
 
A Prompt Code value of 903 is used for Site Configuration Data loads.  This load type is used to 
send the site configuration data tables in a Proprietary Data Load request.  In most cases, this 
will be a multiple message exchange between the Site System and the BUYPASS FEP.   
The Block Number starts at 1 and is incremented with each segment of site configuration data 
as it is sent.  A value of 0 in the Block Number field indicates that all data was sent in the 
previous blocks.  A value of 0 in the Block Number field is sent as a final message and does not 
contain any site configuration data on it. 
Site configuration data is sent to the host when a configuration change occurs at the site.  If 
multiple configuration changes occur at a site during a business day, only the final site 
configuration data is sent to the host.   If no configuration changes occur during a business day, 
then no data is sent from the site to the host. 
The Response Codes for the Site Configuration Data load are: 
• T – Approved—Proprietary load data, no more data pending 
• U – Declined—Proprietary load data, no more data pending

12-43 
12.16.4 Proprietary Load Response Data, Prompt Code 904 
 
A Prompt Code value of 904 is used when the Response Code in a Totals Response indicates 
that proprietary load data is pending.  The device then sends a Proprietary Data Load Request, 
using a Prompt Code value of 904.  Once the device receives the proprietary load response 
data, it then applies the host discount data to applicable transactions during the designated date 
and time period. 
The amount of the discount in a Financial Transaction Request is included in the Product Code 
Data Segment, Segment No. 102 using Product Code 941 or 991. 
Note: Product Code 941 indicates a negative amount and is used in a post-pay environment 
when the discount is applied to the transaction amount. 
 Product Code 991 indicates an administrative amount and is used in a pre-pay 
environment when the price is adjusted to include the discount amount. 
 
The following table illustrates the format of Field Nos. 14-27 when the value of Data Element

12.30 Tax by Product Data Segment 
This section describes Data Segment No.143, Tax by Product Data Segment. 
When a Financial Transaction request includes the Tax by Product Segment, the following rules 
should be followed:  
• A Product Code Data Segment (Data Segment No. 102) must be present in the transaction. 
• Each entry in the Product Code Data Segment (Data Segment No. 102) should have an 
entry in this segment too and the entries should be in the same order in both the segments.  
• Up to three taxes can be reported for a single product. If less than three taxes are to be 
used for a particular product, merchants can end the entry for that product early by using a 
field separator after the tax entry instead of a “\”. 
• If there is no tax associated with a particular product, the inclusive/exclusive flag should be 
set to “N”. In this case, the tax type and amount should be omitted. So, the entry for that 
product would only be the product number, followed by “N”, followed by field separator. 
• The only validation that will be done for this segment is whether the format is correct. No 
judgement will be made of the values contained. 
• For Canadian transactions, the valid values for Tax Type are GST (Goods and Services 
Tax), HST (Harmonized Sales Tax), and PST (Provincial State Tax). Any given product can 
have between 0 and 3 of these taxes specified in this segment. 
 
The following table illustrates the layout of the Tax by Product Segment:  
Notes: A Field Separator always follows Segment Type and Segment Length. A Field Separator 
follows the last Tax Amount for each product.  
A Tax by Product Field Delimiter follows each tax amount when there is another tax amount for 
this product.  
Several examples of the segment accompanied by the Product Code Data Segment follow the 
table.  
In the following table, the ▲ symbol represents a Field Separator, and the \ character is a Tax 
by Product Field Delimiter.

Example:

The product segment contains a single product: 020 for $20.00 
143.023.01020IGST200.

followed by a FS. 
 
102.041.S02963U01\225\25\400U01\2500\500. 
This product segment contains 2 products: 963 and 400. 
143.032.02963N.400EGST25\IPST50. 
In this scenario, product “963” had no taxes associated with it (since it’s already a tax itself), so 
it includes the product. But with an “N” as inclusive/exclusive followed immediately by FS 
indicates end of the process for that product. This is followed by product “400” with an exclusive 
GST of .25 and an inclusive PST of .50. The tax entries are separated by “\” and the whole 
process ends with a FS.

12.31 Enhanced Fleet Request Segment 
This section describes Data Segment No. 145, Enhanced Fleet Request Segment. 
The Enhanced Fleet Request Segment contains fleet data that applies to the enhanced fleet 
offerings such as Wex OTR, Comdata, Voyager EMV, and Visa Fleet 2.0. This segment will 
potentially hold multiple sub-segments, each of which contains different fleet transaction-related 
data. The sub-segments will be in the standard TLV format (sub-segment type, sub-segment 
length, sub-segment value). 
The following table illustrates the layout of the Enhanced Fleet Request Segment: 
Note: Only the Prompt Table sub-segment is valid for the Voyager EMV transactions. 
Note:  Only the Prompt Table sub-segment is valid for Visa Fleet 2.0 transactions. 
Note:  Only the Prompt Table sub-segment is valid for Comdata transactions. 
Note:  Only the Prompt Table sub-segment is valid for MasterCard Enhanced Fleet EMV 
transactions. 
Availability Notice: This functionality for MasterCard Enhanced transactions is expected to be 
enabled in First Data production no earlier than June 2026. Until then, this field is intended for 
development and certification preparation only and should not be used for live production 
transactions. 
Note:  Merchants should not send Fleet segment (Data Segment No. 101) and Enhanced fleet 
segment together (Data Segment No. 145).

TS = Maximum length of the string; an edit mask of X7 indicates 7 as the 
maximum string length 
Vn Validates exact match, where n is the data value to match; an edit mask of 
V1234 indicates that the data value must match 1234 
Pn Validates match against provided pattern, where n is the pattern to match. 
Pattern 
Mask 
 
Description 
@ Position must contain an Alpha character 
# Position must contain a Numeric character 
* Position must contain an Alphanumeric character 
Letter 
or 
Number 
This letter or number is required in this position. 
For example, an edit mask of PUN#### indicates that the data must start with 
“UN” and be followed by four numeric characters.

Reading that is a numeric string between 1 and 25 characters long, and a Unit number that is 
“UN” followed by four digits: 
“004029|DRID:V1100|ODRD:N;TS;M1;X25|UNIT:O;PUN####|”

12-106 
12.41 Adjusted Product Code Data Segment  
This section describes Data Segment No. 157, Adjusted Product Code Data Segment. 
Note:  This segment is used exclusively and allowed for Comdata cards only. Any transaction 
containing this segment that is not for a Comdata card will be declined. 
Note:  This segment is mutually exclusive with segment 102 Product Code Data.  Merchants 
should send one or the other but never both.  If both the segments are sent, the transaction will 
be declined. 
Note: This segment does not allow any product codes above ‘899’ except for ‘955’ Cash Back. 
If any of these product codes is present, the transaction will be declined.  
When a Financial Transaction request includes the Adjusted Product Code Data Segment, the 
products within this segment must meet the following requirements: 
Fuel products must always be the first products in the segment. 
A maximum of ten products is allowed in the segment. 
The total of adjusted product amounts in the segment must equal the total of the amounts 
[Element No. 41 (Fuel Purchase Amount), Element No. 58 (Nonfuel Amount), Element No. 99 
(Tax Amount), and Element No. 17 (Cash Amount)] in the Standard Message Data Segment 
(Data Segment No. 100). 
Since tax amounts are being added to the individual product amounts, there should not be 
separate tax product codes included in the segment.  Instead, tax amount should be reported in 
Element No. 99 (Tax Amount) in the Standard Message Data Segment (Data Segment No. 
100). 
Since Discount, Tax, and Coupon amounts are being accounted for in the individual product 
amounts, there should not be separate discount, tax, or coupon product codes included in the 
segment. 
All fuel merchants must send fuel and nonfuel product data if applicable. 
Note: A unique Product Code must be sent for each type of fuel purchased. 
Note: With the growth of fleet industry and to fulfil the needs of the Over the Road Trucking 
(OTR) industry, BUYPASS can accept transactions with multiple fuels (e.g., purchase of Diesel, 
DEF, REEFER), all in 1 transaction. It is estimated that up to 30% of fuel transactions in OTR 
require fill-ups involving multiple Fuel Type Codes.  Now, fuel merchants can allow multiple fuel 
fill-ups in 1 transaction. With the support of multiple fuels, a merchant must send the Product 
segment to BUYPASS with all the fuel codes and any non-fuel codes with all the relevant 
information like quantity, unit of measure, unit price, and product amount. Also, the merchant 
must send the primary fuel (fuel used for the primary fuel need of the truck/vehicle) as the very 
first product code within the Adjusted Product Code Segment. 
This data segment can appear in any of the fields in Data Section No. 3.  (Please refer to 
section 11.1, “Financial Transactions,” for additional information about Data Section No. 3.) 
It has a maximum length of 381 alphanumeric characters (001–381/a–z/A–Z). 
It originates at the device.

Number: 1 Name: Access Code 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 12 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of up to 12 alphanumeric characters 
Purpose: Identifies data that must be dialed prior to dialing the phone 
number in the Telephone Table Load Response. 
 Examples. PBX access codes 
   Codes for disabling custom calling features 
Processing Rules: If Access Code information is not necessary, the dial string 
contains neither this element nor the Pause Indicator that 
immediately follows it; however, this element may be used to 
indicate a much longer than standard pause for use with phone 
systems that are slow to provide a dial tone.  In these cases, one 
or more B characters may be inserted in this element.  Each one 
should be interpreted as a 1-second pause.

13-24 
Representation: 
 Non-TransArmor—Initial Transaction—Request: 
 Format: 123456789012nn…nn 
 Where 123456789012nn…nn = a variable length (up to 24 alphanumeric 
bytes) Account Number. 
 Non-TransArmor—Initial Transaction—Response: 
 Format: 123456789012nnnnnnnnnnnnn 
 Where 123456789012nnnnnnnnnnnnn = a fixed length (25 alphanumeric bytes) 
Account Number. 
 Non-TransArmor— Subsequent Transaction —Request: 
 Format: 123456789012nn…nn 
 Where 123456789012nn…nn = a variable length (up to 24 alphanumeric 
bytes) Account Number. 
 Non-TransArmor— Subsequent Transaction —Response: 
 Format: 123456789012nnnnnnnnnnnnn 
 Where 123456789012nnnnnnnnnnnnn = a fixed length (25 alphanumeric bytes) 
Account Number. 
 TransArmor – All Messages: 
 For all TransArmor formatting of the Account Number field, see Appendix AA. 
TransArmor Processing Considerations. 
 
Purpose: Non-TransArmor:  Identifies the card or account. 
 TransArmor (Either Encryption Method):  Identifies the 25-byte 
TransArmor header plus the 400-byte EDATA block that contains 
the encrypted/unencrypted information that identifies the account 
for TransArmor. 
  
 
Processing Rules: For non-TransArmor and TransArmor Token Only, the POS 
device maintains the card’s Account Number until it receives a 
response from the host. 
 For TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization, the POS 
device must not maintain the card’s Account Number after the 
initial card swipe. 
 For Non-TransArmor and TransArmor, if the Account Number is 
obtained from a Track 2 card reader, instead of being manually 
keyed, the Account Number and Card Discretionary Block Data 
should consist of all data read from the card between, but not 
including, the Start Sentinel and End Sentinel.  Account Number is 
considered the data before the = character, and Card 
Discretionary Block Data is considered the data after the = 
character.  The = character is used instead of a Field Separator. 
 For Non-TransArmor and TransArmor, if the Account Number is 
obtained from a Track 1 card reader (credit cards only), instead of 
--- PAGE 358 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
13-25 
being manually keyed, the Account Number and Card 
Discretionary Block Data should consist of all unaltered data read 
from the card between, but not including, the Start Sentinel and 
End Sentinel.  Account Number is considered the data before the 
first ^ character, and Card Discretionary Block Data is considered 
the data after the first ^ character.  The ^ character is used instead 
of a Field Separator. For Non-TransArmor – Account Number 
and Card Discretionary Block Data combined do not exceed 76 
bytes for Track 1 or 37 bytes for Track 2. 
 For TransArmor (Either Encryption Method) – Account Number 
and Card Discretionary Block Data combined do not exceed 476 
bytes for Track 1 or Track 2. 
Note: Track data placed in the combined data elements of 
Account Number and Card Discretionary Block Data cannot 
exceed the total length of those data elements 
Real Time Account Updater: 
When a merchant receives Account Updater Card Number (New 
PAN) in the original transaction response in the Real Time 
Account Updater Response Segment – Segment 155, the 
merchant can send either the new PAN or the original PAN in the 
‘Follow-on’ transactions in this Account Number field. 
When a merchant receives Account Updater TransArmor Token 
(New TransArmor Token) in the original transaction response in 
the Real Time Account Updater Response Segment – Segment 
155, the merchant can send either the new TransArmor token or 
the original TransArmor token in the ‘Follow-on’ transactions in 
this Account Number field as TAP request. 
In the event of a ‘Retry’ of a ‘Follow-on’ transaction (Reversals, 
Completions, Cancellations, Void of Merchandise Return, and 
Timeout reversals) by the merchant, the merchant should use the 
same credentials for the retry as were used in the initial attempt.  
Refer to Appendix AD – Real Time Account Updater for more 
details. 
 
 
Valid Codes/Values: Credit, debit, and EBT cards:  Please refer to the most recent 
version of BUYPASS® Platform Issuer Identification Number (IIN) 
Reference Manual. 
Fleet cards:  Please refer to the most recent version of 
BUYPASS® Platform Petroleum Industry Processing 
Specifications. 
Stored Value cards:  The length of the Account Number should 
be 16 or 19 bytes. 
Note: For a First DataTM Premium Gift Card Transaction 
Response, the calculated card number is returned in the 
Account Number field.

Number: 5 Name: Approval Number 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 6 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of six alphanumeric characters; space-filled 
Purpose: Identifies the assigned Approval Number. 
Processing Rules: Required on reversals for matching information to the original 
purchase.  If it is included in a Purchase Request, then the 
Purchase Request is considered preauthorized, and BUYPASS 
does not go out for authorization. 
 In the case of an Authorization Only Reversal, this element—
present in the original transaction—must be present and identical 
in the Authorization Only Reversal transaction.  (Note:  The 
Authorization Only Reversal transaction enables a merchant to 
reverse the following credit card transactions within required 
timeframes:  POS Authorization Only [Transaction Type code 
“3”]); POS Mail/Phone Authorization Only [Transaction Type code 
“B”]); and CAT Authorization Only [Transaction Type code “5”]). 
Valid Codes/Values: Any alphanumeric representation, including spaces 
 
Number:   6 Name:   Approved Amount 
Character Type:  N Maximum Length: 9 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of nine digits with two assumed decimal places 
 Zero-filled and right aligned 
Purpose: Identifies the amount approved by the issuer. 
Processing Rules: The Approved Amount may not be the same as the requested 
amount. 
 If the transaction is run from an AFP device, the pump should be 
set to pump the Approved Amount—not the requested amount. 
 If the transaction is a Partial Approval transaction, the amount 
approved is contained in this field, and the POS device must 
prompt for payment of the remaining balance due in the sale. 
Valid Codes/Values: 000000001–999999999

Number: 11 Name: Block Number 
Character Type:  N Maximum Length: 3 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of three digits 
Purpose: Identifies the specific proprietary or public key data block requested 
by a device or sent by the host. 
Processing Rules: The host always uses a Block Number to track the data block it 
sends in an Electronic Mail response and a CA Public Key File 
Load response.  If response processing is interrupted, the host 
knows the Block Number for the last complete data block sent in 
the response. 
 A device is not required to track the Block Number it receives in 
an Electronic Mail response.  If it is required to do so, and 
processing between the host and device is interrupted, the device 
can reinstate transmission of the interrupted data block using that 
Block Number in the next Electronic Mail request it sends to the 
host. 
 A device always uses a Block Number to track the data block it 
sends in a Proprietary Data Load request.  If request processing is 
interrupted, the host knows the Block Number for the last 
complete data block sent in the request. 
 A device is required to track the Block Number it receives in a CA 
Public Key File Load response.  If CA Public Key File Load 
processing between the host and device is interrupted, the device 
reinstates transmission of the interrupted data block using that 
Block Number in the next request it sends to the host. 
Valid Codes/Values: Codes Description 
000 The host sends the first data block for CA 
Public Key File Load. 
000 The device sends this value indicating the 
last block of site / fuel volume data is being 
sent in the Proprietary Data Load request. 
001 The host restarts data block processing, 
and sends the block that was Block No. 1 in 
the Electronic Mail response as the next 
block. 
 <specific Block No.> The device can request a particular block by 
sending that Block Number in the next 
Electronic Mail request or CA Public Key 
File Load request.

Number: 63 Name: Number of Segments 
Character Type: N Maximum Length: 2 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of up to two digits 
Purpose: Identifies the number of BUYPASS-defined data segments 
included in the Financial Transaction Request, Totals Request, 
Loyalty Card Transaction Request, and Electronic Mail Request. 
Processing Rules: It originates at the device. 
 Financial Transaction Requests:  This data element is always 
followed by Data Section No. 2 which contains Data Segment No. 
100, Standard Message Data Segment, plus Data Section No. 3 
which contains none, one, or more of the of the input data 
segments listed in Chapter 12. 
 Loyalty Card Transaction Requests:  This data element is 
always followed by Data Section No. 2 which contains Data 
Segment No. 100, Standard Message Data Segment, plus Data 
Section No. 3 which contains Data Segment No. 108, Loyalty 
Card Data Segment, and Data Segment 114, SKU Data Segment. 
 ECA/ TeleCheck® Service Transaction Requests:  This data 
element is always followed by Data Section No. 2 which contains 
Data Segment No. 100, Standard Message Data Segment, plus 
Data Section No. 3 which contains Data Segment No. 110, Check 
Data Segment, and Data Segment 111, Variable Information Data 
Segment. 
 Totals Requests:  This data element is always followed by Data 
Segment No. 105, Totals Data Segment. 
 Electronic Mail Requests:  This data element is always followed 
by Data Section No. 2, which contains Data Segment No. 109, 
Electronic Mail Data Segment. 
 Communications Test Requests:  This data element is always 
followed by Data Section No. 2 which contains Element No. 120, 
Network Management Message. 
 TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization:  This data 
element is used for a Key and Key ID Load.  In the requests, it is 
always followed by Data Section No. 2, which contains Data 
Segment No. 116, TransArmor Load Data Segment. 
 
Valid Codes/Values: The value of this field, call it N, indicates that the transaction will 
 have the 100 segment + N-1 of the input segments listed in 
 Chapter 12.
