Number: 77 Name: Product Code 
Character Type: N Maximum Length: 3 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of three digits 
Purpose: Identifies the type of product in Data Segment No. 102, Product 
Code Data Segment or Data Segment No. 157, Adjusted Product 
Code Data Segment.  
 In the case of a Proprietary Load Response (Prompt Code 904), 
the first instance identifies the type of product which is eligible for

• Quantity (No. 81)

• Product Amount (No. 76) 
Note: A unique Product Code must be sent for each type of fuel 
purchase. 
 When a device uses a Dynamic Card Table, only the product 
codes defined in the table are valid for transaction processing.  
 In the case of a Proprietary Load Response (Host Discount Data, 
Prompt Code 904), the value in the second or third positions of the 
Product Code may contain a wild card character of *.  If that 
occurs, any digit is allowed in that position.  For example, if the 
value is 01*, product codes 010, 011, 012, 013, 014, 015, 016, 
017, 018 and 019 are all available for discount. 
Valid Codes/Values: Please refer to Appendix F.  Valid Payment Systems Product

Number: 105 Name: Totals Date 
Character Type: N Maximum Length: 6 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of six digits

 MMDDYY YYMMDD Identifies a request for totals for a

 111111 111111 Identifies a request for totals for the 
period of time since the last 999999 
code was used. 
 222222 YYMMDD Identifies a request for totals for the 
current settlement date; ends the 
current settlement date; and rolls the 
date to the next settlement date. 
 333333 YYMMDD Identifies a request for totals for the 
most recent date with activity. 
 444444 YYMMDD Identifies a request for totals for the 
second most recent date with 
activity. 
 555555 YYMMDD Identifies a request for totals for the 
third most recent date with activity. 
 999999 999999 Identifies a request to clear all totals 
since the last 999999 code was 
used.  Used with the 111111 code.

Number: 113 Name: Variable Information 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 982 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of up to 982 alphanumeric characters 
 Note: Please refer to section 12.10, “Variable Information Data 
Segment,” for conditions affecting this element’s length. 
Purpose: Identifies the data in a Variable Information Data Segment. 
Processing Rules: Used in the Variable Information Data Segment (No. 111). 
 When Element No. 111 (Variable Information Indicator) has a value 
of 001 (UPC indicator), the actual UPC is included here. 
 When Element No. 111 (Variable Information Indicator) has a value 
of 002 (Program Identifier Indicator), the actual 3-byte Program 
Identifier is included here. 
 When Element No. 111 (Variable Information Indicator) has a value 
of 003 (AVS indicator), address information (street name, ZIP 
Code™/ZIP+4®) is included here. 
 When Element No. 111 (Variable Information Indicator) has a value 
of 004 [card verification value (CVV, CVV2, CVC2, CID) indicator], 
the card’s actual verification code is included here. 
 When Element No. 111 (Variable Information Indicator) has a value 
of 005 (point-of-service entry mode indicator), the actual point-of-
service entry mode (swiped/manual/RFID) is included here. 
 When Element No. 111 (Variable Information Indicator) has a value 
of 006 (currency code indicator), the actual currency code (always 
3 bytes) is included here. 
 When Element No. 111 (Variable Information Indicator) has a value 
of 007 (SIC indicator), the actual SIC (4 or 5 or 6 numeric bytes) is 
included here. 
 When Element No. 111 (Variable Information Indicator) has a value 
of 008 (balance transfer—stored value card account number 
indicator), the account number (maximum of 19 digits) of the 
account that is being reduced to $0.00 is included here. 
 When Element No. 111 (Variable Information Indicator) has a value 
of 009 (Partial Approval Indicator), the Partial Approval Indicator 
(fixed length of 1 alphanumeric characters) is included here. 
 When Element No. 111 (Variable Information Indicator) has a value 
of 010 (Visa® Trusted Agent Program (TAP) Indicator), the Visa® 
Trusted Agent Program (TAP) Indicator is included here. 
 When Element No. 111 (Variable Information Indicator) has a value 
of 011 (Tax Collector Indicator), the code indicating whether the 
transaction is taxable and whether sales tax is included is included 
here.

Number: 121 Name: Partial Approval 
Indicator 
Character Type: N Maximum Length: 1 byte 
 
Representation: Fixed length of 1 digit 
Purpose: Indicates whether or not a merchant supports credit/debit/fleet 
Partial Approvals. 
Processing Rules: Required on all transactions. 
Valid Codes/Values: Value Description 
0 Not specified (default)/Not supported 
 This value is the default value. 
 If the Merchant does not support credit/debit/fleet 
Partial Approvals, then this value is transmitted. 
 1 Supported 
This value indicates that the Merchant supports 
credit/debit/fleet Partial Approval transactions. 
If the Merchant transmits this value with a 
transaction—and the corresponding network 
supports credit/debit/fleet Partial Approval 
transactions—the network can approve an amount 
that is less than the amount in the Authorization 
request; and BUYPASS will send a Partial Approval 
response. 
The network may return a card balance that is 
printed on the customer’s copy of the receipt. 
 5 This value indicates that the Merchant only 
supports the receipt of the card balance, not Partial 
Approval transaction processing. 
The network may return a card balance that is 
printed on the customer’s copy of the receipt. 
Note: This value is only supported for American 
Express prepaid cards. 
Note: Support for Partial Authorization is mandatory for all card brands. Data Element 121 ( 
Partial Approval Indicator) should be populated correctly for all card present transactions, 
showing that the terminal is capable of partial authorization responses. 
Note: For American Express transactions, Merchants sending transaction request amount as 
‘zero’ and using values ‘1’ or ‘5’ for Prepaid card balances, will not be receiving the card balance 
back in response.

Number: 154 Name: WIC Product Data 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 3001 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of up to 3,001 alphanumeric characters 
Purpose: Identifies data unique to eWIC transactions. 
Processing Rules: Appears in EBT Data Segment (Segment No. 103). 
 Composed of two or more of the following subelements: 
• Total Length 
• One or more of the following: 
• Earliest WIC Benefit Expiration Date 
• WIC Prescription Balance Information 
• WIC UPC Exception/Denial Information 
• WIC UPC Purchase Information 
Earliest WIC Benefit Expiration Date is included in the eWIC 
Balance Inquiry Response, eWIC Authorization Response, and 
eWIC Purchase Completion Response. 
WIC Prescription Balance is included in the eWIC Balance Inquiry 
Response, eWIC Authorization Response, eWIC Purchase 
Completion Response. 
For WIC purchases involving fruits and vegetables via the Cash 
Value Benefit (CVB), please set the Quantity equal to the price in 
the WIC Purchase Information. 
WIC UPC Exception/Denial Information is included in the eWIC 
Purchase Completion Response, and eWIC Voucher Clear 
Response. 
In cases where the WIC Purchase price exceeds the value set by 
the state (and provided in the Approved Product List [APL] file), an 
exception record is returned in the WIC Product Data field.  The 
exception record reflects both the approved and original prices for 
the transaction.  The total transaction amount (Settlement 
Amount) is adjusted to reflect the total price adjustments, and is 
returned in the Approved Amount field.

Number: 190 Name: EMV Chip Data 
Character Type: ANSB Maximum Length: 999 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of 999 characters, preceded by three digit length 
indicator 
 All fields after the table length are in binary format. 
Purpose: Identifies the data sent in the EMV card to terminal interface. 
Processing Rules: Required in all EMV transactions. 
 EMV data elements include a series of TLV (Tag/Length/Value) 
combinations which are required for processing EMV transactions. 
 All data elements must contain the exact values that were present on 
the card to terminal interface. 
 If the same data element appears several times on the card to 
terminal interface, this field must contain the last value that was 
present on the card to terminal interface during the transaction. 
 Note: For the EMV transaction to be processed properly, the 
Application ID (AID) TLV (tag 9F06) or Dedicated File Name (tag 84) 
must be included in Data Element No. 190 (EMV Chip Data). 
Note: Tag ‘5A’ (PAN) and Tag ‘57’ (Track 2 equivalent data) must not 
be included in Data Element 190 — EMV Chip Data. 
Valid Codes/Values: The components of EMV data elements are described below: 
Component Name:  Tag 
Each sub element or Tag can be either one or two bytes long.  To 
determine the length, check the last five bits of the first byte, if they 
are all on (1) the tag of the sub element is two bytes long, including 
the current byte. 
Example 1: Tag x’9F10’ is a two byte tag - the last five bits of 
the first byte (x’9F’) are all ones. 
Example 2: Tag x’72’ is a one byte tag - the last five bits of the 
first byte (x’72’) are not all ones. 
Component Name:  Length (ANSB …127) 
The next one or more bytes are the length indicator of the tag.  To 
determine the number of length bytes used for this inspect the first 
byte of the length field.  If the first bit of the first byte is a 1, the 
remaining bits (next seven) are a binary representation of the number 
of following bytes of the length field.  If the first bit is 0, the remaining 
bits indicate the actual length of the data that follows.  
Example 1: If the length byte is x’0C’, then 12 is the length of 
the data that follows the sub element. 
Example 2: If the tag is x’82’, the length is contained in the next 
byte of the sub element. The value in the length byte 
indicates the number of bytes of data following. 
--- PAGE 472 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
13-139 
Component Name:  Value (ANSB …255) 
The data of each Tag/Length/Value combination is up to 255 bytes 
long, depending on the length of the field specified by the preceding 
length portion of the sub element.  
For an example of this data element, please see Appendix R.  EMV 
Chip Data.

 Note: The device concatenates all of the CA Public Key File Block 
data to construct the CA Public Key File. 
 For a declined EMV load transaction, a message is returned in this 
field and displays at the device. 
Valid Codes/Values: Any valid key. 
 Following are the error codes that are returned in the terminal: 
 Code     Description 
 RQST/CURRENT HASH MATCH Key update not required 
 BLOCK NBR NOT NUMERIC  Key load transaction not  
   successful 
 BLOCK NBR NOT 000-xxx  Key load transaction not  
   successful 
 Please refer to Appendix S.  Valid CA Public Key File Record Layout.

Number: 196 Name: Token Requestor ID 
Character Type: AN Max. Length: 11 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of 11 bytes 
Purpose: Identifies merchant’s Token Requestor ID. 
Processing Rules: This Data Element is used only for Visa/MasterCard payment 
tokenized transactions. 
Valid Codes/Values: Position        Description 
                                               1-11               Token Requestor ID, Left justified, space-filled 
Note: In late 2014, MasterCard introduced the Card on File 
tokenization service and static card on file token type to support 
token payments for e-Commerce merchants that traditionally 
stored credit card numbers.  MasterCard required merchants to 
submit the Token Requestor ID for Card on File tokenized 
transactions.  Effective 8 June 2021, MasterCard renamed the 
Card on File token type to “Static Token” type.  Also, they 
removed the requirement to submit the Token Requestor ID. 
However, if submitted, MasterCard will validate and will decline if 
invalid.  
Merchants are advised not to send the Token Requestor ID if 
submitting a Card on File tokenized transaction/Static Token type.  
Cryptographic Data is still not required for Static Tokens.   
Merchants that submit Secure Element and Cloud-based token 
types are still required to submit the Token Requestor ID along 
with Cryptographic data, if applicable.

Number: 198 Name: Settlement Type

 Value Description

 X  Transaction was processed Dual message (non-traditional  
   Signature Debit) 
 Note: In EMV transactions, if ‘D’ is returned in response, then 
 subsequent transactions i.e. completion or void or reversal must be 
 sent as credit. This will be reflected in the Prompt Code (Data 
 segment 100: Data Element 78) of the subsequent transaction. 
   In EMV transactions, if ‘S’ is returned in response, then 
 subsequent transactions i.e. completion or void or reversal must be 
 sent as debit. This will be reflected in the Prompt Code (Data segment 
 100: Data  Element 78) of the subsequent transaction.

14-1 
14. Support, Testing, and Certification 
This chapter discusses the following topics: 
• Project management 
• Development support 
• General testing  
• Certification 
14.1 Project Management 
BUYPASS uses a project management process.  One of the main objectives of the process is to 
provide the best definition possible of the customer’s requirements.  A customer project is 
submitted by a sponsor for approval.  When a project has been approved, a project leader is 
assigned.  The project sponsor identifies a customer representative who is included in meetings 
and receives project updates.  The customer representative works with the project sponsor to 
construct the requirement document and identify critical benchmarks.  The customer 
representative also works with the functional areas involved in the project itself.  The actual 
management of the project takes place at BUYPASS. 
14.2 Development Support 
Support is available for BUYPASS customers before, during, and after implementation of the 
interface between a customer’s device and BUYPASS. 
--- PAGE 495 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
14-2 
14.3 General Testing 
BUYPASS provides a QA test system for the customer, vendor, or third-party processor to test 
new software code, modifications/enhancements to existing software code, communications, 
host interface functions, and other general testing prior to scheduling certification time. 
The client is assigned a test BUYPASS Merchant Number and access number to interface to 
the test system.  Support by BUYPASS QA analysts is available. 
General testing includes the following areas: 
• Telecommunications 
 Connections 
 Line down 
• Message formats 
 Requests 
• Transaction types 
• Card types 
 Responses 
• Authorizer-generated for approved transactions 
• Authorizer-generated for denied transactions 
• Transactions denied by BUYPASS 
14.4 Certification 
A customer, vendor, or third-party processor is required to submit a Request for Certification 
form once general testing is completed.  This form can be obtained by contacting the BUYPASS 
QA department.  It provides the BUYPASS QA department with the pertinent information 
needed to coordinate and schedule certification time. 
The certification process includes test plans and scripts, designed for the specific application 
requirements of the customer, vendor, or third-party processor.  A BUYPASS QA analyst is 
assigned to the certification and provides support throughout the process. 
The scope of the certification may also require regression testing.  Regression testing is a 
variation of certification testing.

Appendix A-1 
Appendix A.  TCP/IP Message Header 
TCP/IP is a streaming protocol, meaning that data received may consist of part of a message or 
parts of more than one message. 
Example. Message 1: “Hello, I am message one.” 
 Message 2: “Message 2 is my name.” 
 Message 3: “A third message I am.” 
Each time a receive is performed, one or more parts of these messages may be received: 
Example. Receive results 1: “Hello, I” 
 Receive results 2: “ am message one.Mes” 
 Receive results 3: “sage 2 is my name.A thi” 
 Receive results 4: “rd message I am.” 
With no header or delimiter between each message, it is not possible to determine where one 
message ends and another begins.  A simple delimiter such as a carriage return character 
would work well for messages that consist entirely of printable text: 
Example. Message 1: “Hello, I am message one.\n” 
 Message 2: “Message 2 is my name.\n” 
 Message 3: “A third message I am.\n” 
BUYPASS has chosen the standard header method as described below. 
BUYPASS Header 
Field Name Size Description 
Message Length 2 bytes (16 bits) Length of the following data.  High 
order byte is first (network or “big-
endian order”). 
TPDU Protocol ID 1 byte 0x60 (Always use this value.) 
TPDU Destination Address 2 bytes (16 bits) Reserved for internal use. 
TPDU Source Address 2 bytes (16 bits) Reserved for internal use. 
 
--- PAGE 497 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
Appendix A-2 
The message length includes the length of all subsequent data in the message including the 
TPDU area, but does not include the two bytes of the message length itself.  The message 
length is binary data, represented in network (a.k.a. little-endian) order.  Be aware that some 
processor architecture, such as the Intel® processors used on PC's store 16-bit integers in “little-
endian” order, so the bytes should be reversed before sending or after receiving. 
Example. A 4660-byte message would have a length of 0x1234 in hexadecimal.  The first 
byte in the header should contain 0x12 and the second byte should contain 0x34.  
Be aware that a 16-bit integer with a value of 4660 may be represented internally 
on your architecture as 0x3412, so moving this integer directly into or out of the 
message length field would not work. 
The sockets library on your system may have built-in library functions to convert to and from 
network order and the local host order on your machine. 
Note: The TCP/IP socket aborts without notification. 
Also be aware that the streaming nature of TCP may cause your application to receive the 
beginning of a message that contains only one byte of the length.  The actual length of the next 
message will not be known until more data, containing the second byte of the length, is 
received. 
The TPDU area is reserved for internal use.  Set all four bytes to 0x00 in messages to 
BUYPASS. 
Testing may be performed against BUYPASS certification system using the private BUYPASS 
IP network. 
Note: Check with BUYPASS Communications Support at the time of installation for the IP 
address to be used.

Appendix G-1 
 
Appendix G.  Valid Transaction Type Codes 
This appendix contains a list of valid Transaction Type codes. 
Note: This note is specific to merchants processing MasterCard transactions: 
Transactions routed to MasterCard will be defined as Pre Auth or Final as per MasterCard’s 
request. The BUYPASS transactions submitted as Authorization/Completion/Auth Cancellation 
will be presented as Preauthorization* to MasterCard and transactions submitted as Sale/Sale 
Reversals/Merchandise Return/Void of Merchandise Return will be presented as Final 
Authorization** to MasterCard.  
* Preauthorization is a request for an estimated amount, the amount of the original authorization 
may be adjusted if the final transaction amount is different than the original authorization 
amount requested, or the transaction might not be completed for reasons other than technical 
failure or lack of full issuer approval. 
** Final authorization is a request for an amount greater than zero, where the final transaction 
amount is known, and the transaction is not expected to be canceled after the authorization 
request is approved in full.  
MasterCard is revising the chargeback protection period for authorizations. Following are the 
revised chargeback protection period: 
• 30 calendar days for MasterCard authorizations properly identified as preauthorization 
• 7 calendar days for all other MasterCard authorizations  
• Authorization holds must not exceed 30 or 7 calendar days durations as mentioned above 
Note: For a list of valid Card Type codes, please see Appendix E.  Valid Card Type Codes. 
Prompt Codes are transmitted by a device at the time a transaction is initiated.  A valid Prompt 
Code (Element No. 78) is composed of a Transaction Type code and a Card Type code. 
Note: Any Prompt Code beginning with Transaction Type code 9 (See table below.) denotes a 
special transaction, not a financial transaction.  Transaction Type code 9 can only be 
combined with Card Type codes 00 and 81–97. 
The Transaction Type code (one character) identifies the type of transaction being processed. 
The following table contains a list of valid 1-character Transaction Type codes: 
Valid Transaction Type Codes 
Code Transaction Type Transaction Description 
0 POS Purchase/Capture Point-of-sale purchase/preauthorized 
completion 
Note: This Transaction Type code is also 
used to complete an AFP prepay 
transaction initiated from an inside POS 
device. 
3 POS Authorization Only Point-of-sale authorization only (no draft 
capture) 
4 Customer-activated Purchase/Capture Customer-activated purchase completion 
5 Customer-activated Authorization Only Customer-activated authorization only (no 
draft capture) 
6 Mail/Phone Purchase Mail/Telephone order

Card Verification Information 
Field Attributes Description 
Table ID n Fixed value:  004 
Table Length n Variable 
Table Data n Max. Len.:  4 
American Express:  4 bytes 
Discover® Network: 3 bytes 
Visa®:  3 bytes 
MasterCard:  3 bytes 
 
Note: 
For Visa, this field is also used to send three-digit 
DTVV (Dynamic token verification value) cryptogram 
for Web browser based Auto fill transactions, 
alongside CVV2 data. 
Note: 
Web Browser Auto Filling of Tokens (Visa Only): 
Cardholders participating in e-commerce transactions may use web browsers that offer auto-fill 
features, including the ability to auto fill cardholder names, shipping and billing addresses, and 
payment credentials to facilitate cardholder convenience and reduce the possibility of 
incorrectly entering account and payment information. 
To enable increased security of sensitive cardholder information and authorization rates, 
certain card brands allow web browsers to replace PANs with e-commerce tokens, which 
provides cardholders the ability to auto fill token, token expiration date, and three-digit DTVV 
cryptogram on merchant card entry forms. 
To help facilitate seamless payment experiences for cardholders, tokens provisioned by web 
--- PAGE 548 ---
BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
 August 07, 2026 
Appendix I-6 
browsers will: 
• Use a three-digit DTVV cryptogram which is collected by merchants that support CVV2 
and sent in the same manner as a CVV2. 
• Support transactions without a token cryptogram, for scenarios where the merchant 
does not collect and submit CVV2.  
• When a DTVV is present in the authorization request Visa will validate it and decline 
the transaction if invalid.  
• When a DTVV is not present Visa will send the transaction to the issuer to make the 
authorization decision without a cryptogram validation result.

Visa® Trusted Agent Program (TAP) Information 
Field Attributes Description 
Table ID n3 Fixed value:  010 
Table Length an3 Fixed value:  030 
Identifies TAP code for Visa®. 
Positions 1–10:  Visa® BID Value in hexadecimal 
representation (binary 40; Zero-filled, if not used and 
Visa TAP or First Data TPP/VAR ID data is included). 
Positions 11–22:  Visa® TAP Value in hexadecimal 
representation (binary 48; Zero-filled, if not used and 
Visa BID or First Data TPP/VAR ID data is included). 
Positions 23–28:  First Data Corporation TPP (third 
party processor)/VAR (value added reseller) ID 
(alphanumeric 6)  (Note:  Once this ID has been 
assigned, the vendor must send it to BUYPASS in 
Data Segment No. 111 [Variable Information Data 
Segment] of all transaction requests.) 
Positions 29–30:  Reserved for future use 
(alphanumeric 2; space-filled)

 Once certified, the respective terminal capability values do not change   
 regardless of the POS Entry Mode. 
 Valid codes/values: 
 00 = Unknown or unspecified 
 01 = Terminal not used (Example: eCommerce and In App) 
 02 = Magnetic stripe read capability (no contact or contactless chip) 
 03 = Bar code capability 
 04 = Optical character recognition (OCR) read capability 
 05 = Integrated circuit card (ICC) read capability 
 06 = Contactless chip read capability (no contact chip) 
 07 = Contactless magnetic stripe read capability (no contact or 
 contactless chip capability) 
 09 = Terminal does not read card data 
 12 = Hybrid Integrated Circuit Card Reader (Contact Chip &    
            Contactless Chip) Capabilities

Sub Table ID “12” 
Purpose:  Identifies the Alternate Routing Fallback Indicator for Debit Card Not Present (CNP) 
Ecommerce transactions. 
 
Field Attributes Description 
Sub-
Table 
ID 
n2 Fixed Value: 12 
Sub-
Table  
Length 
n3 Fixed Len.: 001 
Sub-
Table  
Data   
an1 Alternate Routing Fallback Indicator is used by merchants to fall back on 
Credit rails when Debit routing is not available for Debit CNP Ecommerce 
transactions.  If debit routing is not available, then the transaction will be 
rerouted to credit or declined based on the value chosen. 
➢ This field is optional with value “Y” if the merchant opts for the 
ability to route the transaction to the credit association when the 
transaction cannot be routed to Debit network. 
 
➢ If the transaction needs to be processed through debit only and 
should not be eligible for credit routing as fallback, then Merchant 
must send value “N” in this indicator.  
 
Valid Code/Value:  
“Y” – Alternate Routing supported (Transaction can be routed to credit 
when debit route is not available) 
“N” – Alternate Routing not supported (Transaction should NOT be 
routed to credit and should be declined when no debit routes available) 
 
Example 1: 111+022+03200612001Y+  
Example 2: 111+022+03200612001N+  
 
Note – When merchant is not sending the indicator, the value “Y” will be 
assumed by default.

Appendix I-33 
Table 
Data 
an Variable length, either 3 or 35 characters. Maximum Len. : 35 
MasterCard UCAF Data contains the following information: 
UCAF Security Level (3 characters). Valid values for UCAF Security 
Level are:   
Valid values for Positions 1–2: 
21 = Channel encryption; cardholder certificate is not used. This is the 
 preferred value.  
24 = Digital secure remote payment with UCAF data transactions.  
Valid values for Position 3: 
0 = UCAF data collection is not supported.  
1 = UCAF data collection is supported; however, UCAF data was not 
 populated.  
2 = UCAF data collection is supported; and UCAF data is present.  
3 = MARP static authentication.  
4 =       MasterCard Identity Check Insights. Merchant has chosen to 
 share authentication data within authorization.  
5 = Issuer risk based decisioning.  
6 = Merchant risk based decisioning.  
7 = Partial shipment or recurring payment. Liability will depend on 
 the original UCAF values provided and match with the initial 
 transaction. 
Note: As more transactions move from traditional web browsers to 
digital platforms and devices, the need to capture additional data for 
sophisticated intelligence is necessary.  Enhancements in technology, 
artificial intelligence, and the EMV 3D Secure standardization have 
enabled MasterCard to improve their Decision Intelligence product suite. 
Identity Check Insights, formerly known as “Data only”, allows merchants 
to share data through the EMV 3DS network to generate authentication 
insights that could influence the issuer’s decisions to approve without 
authentication.  There is no fraud liability shift to the issuer in an Identity 
Check Insight transaction message because the issuer is not receiving 
an authentication request.

Restrictions supported.

RBI recurring mandate for Visa transactions 
 
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mandates that when a cardholder first registers and transacts with a 
merchant, to subsequently have recurring payments debited from the card, additional factor 
authentication is required. For subsequent recurring transactions, additional factor authentication is not 
required.  However, if a cardholder modifies or revokes a standing instruction, additional factor 
authentication is required. 
Merchants are encouraged to subscribe to the Global BIN File for accurate identification of accounts 
issued from India. 
All Visa recurring transactions for cards issued in India must contain new additional recurring data 
contained in Table ID 56 and 013 under Data Element No. 111. 
Subsequent recurring transactions can only be performed for those cards, which have been successfully 
registered, and for which the first transaction was successfully authenticated and authorized.  
 The amount limit for Visa recurring transactions without additional factor authentication is equivalent to 
15,000 INR (might change if the RBI mandate is revised in future). Transactions above the limit will 
--- PAGE 606 ---

Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
 August 07, 2026 
Appendix I-64 
require additional factor authentication and electronic commerce identification.

Appendix I-79 
Table 
Data 
An005 For Visa and Interlink, this field contains a 5-byte network-assigned value that is 
used by networks to identify enablers. 
 
A ‘Visa Enabler Verification Value’ (EVV) is a unique identifier assigned by Visa 
to a third-party payment processor, known as an ‘Enabler’. It is a code used to 
verify the legitimacy of an enabler when processing Visa transactions.  
 
Note: Enablers are payment processing entities that are not acquiring members 
and are often the primary relationship owner with merchants and originators. 
Enablers own technical solutions through which the merchant or originator will 
access acceptance. 
 
 
Example: 111+020+0710053202+ 
 
Note:  Applicable to Visa and Interlink only.

Appendix J-1 
Appendix J.  Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes 
This appendix lists valid entries for Variable Information (Element No. 113). 
A valid 3-digit Point-of-Service Entry Mode code has the following components: 
• 2-digit PAN Entry Mode code in position nos. 1–2 
• 1-digit Terminal Capability Mode code in position no. 3 
The following table contains valid PAN Entry Mode codes: 
Note: The POS Entry Mode values listed below must persist throughout the lifecycle of the 
transactions, except as noted below the Valid PAN Entry Mode Codes table. 
Valid PAN Entry Mode Codes 
Pos. Nos. 1–2 Description 
00 Unspecified 
01 Manual/keyed 
02 Magnetic stripe read with partial track data1 sent to the host 
04 Bar Code Scan 
Optical character recognition (OCR) read for EMV 
05 Integrated circuit card (ICC) read – CVV data reliable (used for EMV chip 
read) 
07 Contactless chip read (used for contactless chip) 
10 Credential on file2 
79 Contact and Contactless chip fallback to manual 
80 Chip card capable – unaltered track data read (used for contact EMV fall 
back to swiped) 
82 Contactless mobile commerce device3 
86 Dual interface contactless chip to contact chip 
90 Magnetic stripe read with full track data1 sent to the host 
91 Full contactless magnetic stripe read with track data1 sent to the host 
95 Integrated circuit card (ICC) read – CVV data unreliable 
1Due to credit authorizer (American Express, Diners Club®, Discover® Network, JCB®, MasterCard®, MasterCard® Fleet, 
Visa®, and Visa® Fleet) and debit authorizer regulatory requirements regarding storage of full track data, previously authorized 
credit and debit transactions (Voids and Completions) can only pass the account number and expiration date to BUYPASS.  These 
transactions will use the same PAN Entry Mode code as their corresponding original Purchase or Authorization transaction, with one 
exception:  They will use a PAN Entry Mode code 02 when referencing an original Purchase or Authorization transaction in which a 
PAN Entry Mode code 90 was used. 
 
2Entry Mode 10 is applicable  to Visa Credit, MasterCard Credit, Discover Credit, and Amex transactions where merchant or 
cardholder is initiating a transaction based on the credentials already stored on the file. The value is also applicable to the 
subsequent Debit Completions and Debit Reversals when the original transaction was initiated as a Credit COF transaction. The 
value is NOT applicable to the first transaction where credentials are being verified or stored.  For Discover, POS Entry Mode ‘10’ 
must NOT be present in the following scenarios: 
• QR Code/Bar Code/Payment Code transactions 
• Card Sales with card account information stored by an Issuer or provisioned in a digital wallet  
3For Discover, Entry Mode 82 must NOT be assigned to card transactions for which the cardholder uses their stored card account 
information. Discover Credential on File transactions must use the POS Entry Mode value of '10'.

Appendix J-2 
 
The following table contains valid Terminal PIN Entry Capability Mode codes: 
Valid Terminal PIN Entry Capability Mode Codes1 
Position 3 Description 
0 Unspecified 
1 PIN entry capability (including both EMV Contact and Contactless) 
2 No PIN entry capability (including both EMV Contact and Contactless) 
3  mPOS Software-based PIN Entry Capability 
6 PIN pad inoperative 
8 Contactless Magnetic Stripe Read Capability 
1If more than one valid Terminal Capability Mode code exists for a POS device, the following hierarchy logic should be followed: 
If a Contactless MSR is attached to the POS device and it has no chip capability, then all transactions will use Terminal PIN Entry 
Capability Mode code 8; but 
For EMV Contact and Contactless the valid PIN Entry Capability Mode code is 1 and not 8. The PIN Entry Capability Mode code 8 is 
reserved only for Contactless MSR; or 
If no Contactless MSR is attached, and the POS device has the PIN debit feature enabled, then all transactions will use Terminal 
PIN Entry Capability Mode code 1; or 
If no Contactless MSR is attached, and the POS device has the PIN debit feature disabled, then all transactions will use Terminal 
PIN Entry Capability Mode code 2. 
PIN entry capability mode code 3 is applicable only to MasterCard Mobile POS transactions. 
mPOS transactions can be classified based on the presence of PIN pad (Hardware-based) or without PIN pad (Software-based).   
mPOS Devices Phone/Tablet + Dongle with PIN Pad should have PIN Entry Capability Mode code as 1.  
mPOS Devices Phone/Tablet + Dongle without PIN Pad should have PIN Entry Capability Mode code as 3.

Visa network if the merchant sends Table ID 34 (NVS Information) in 
Variable information segment 111 for a verification transaction. 
 
It contains 3 bytes of data. Below are the valid values for all the 3 bytes 
of data. First byte refers to the Account nume match decision for First 
Name. 
Second byte refers to the account name match decision for Last name. 
Third byte refers to the account name match decision for Middle name. 
 
The valid values are: 
M  - Match 
P  - Partial Match 
N   - No Match 
SPACES – Not applicable or name match decision not received from 
Visa network.

Example.  02450209850840C000000001234 
 
Valid Codes/Values for the Element when Used in A Request Containing a HIP 
Purchase/Return Amount 
Data Description 
Subelement 1:  Total Length 
024 Total Length of all data in the entire message 
Format:  n3; right-aligned; zero-filled 
The value “024” indicates that 24 characters follow. 
Subelement 2:  Program Data 
50 New Label:  TAG (Indicates the type of HIP data to follow.) 
Format:  n2 
The value “50” indicates a HIP purchase/return amount follows. 
20 New Label:  LEN (Indicates the length of the Detail data to follow. 
Format:  n2 
The value “020” indicates that 20 characters follow.

Appendix O-1 
 
Appendix O.  Payment Token Terminologies 
This appendix contains a list of general terminologies related to payment tokenization 
transactions.  
Payment Tokenization Terminologies and Descriptions 
Term Description 
Cryptogram 
Token Data 
In App transactions coming from merchants will be sent with security data 
that contains In App token cryptogram. 
Merchant can send 28 bytes or 56 bytes of Cryptogram Data in base64 
format.  
If merchant sends 56 bytes of token data, then BUYPASS considers it as 
token data block A and token data block B.  
If merchant sends only 28 bytes of token data, then BUYPASS considers it 
as token data block A. 
Payment Token A surrogate value for a PAN is generated by and maintained in the token 
vault. This value is consistent with BUYPASS Platform (BUYPASS).message 
requirements, and is a 13 to 19-digit numeric value that must pass basic 
validation rules of an account number, including the LUHN check. Payment 
tokens are generated within a BIN range that has been designated as a 
token BIN range and flagged accordingly in all appropriate BIN tables. 
Payment tokens must not have the same value as a cardholder PAN. 
Payment Token 
Expiration Date 
The expiration date of the token is populated in the PAN Expiration Date field 
during transaction processing to ensure interoperability and minimize the 
impact of tokenization implementation. 
Payment Token 
Requestor 
Enrolled entity requesting payment token PANs for initiating payments. 
Example: Merchants, Vendors, Aggregators, Acquirers, etc. 
Payment Token 
Service 
Provider 
The operator of the token vault which is the licensed BIN provider; Example: 
Card brand networks, Issuers etc. 
POS Entry 
Mode 
A value that is used to indicate the token presentment mode through which 
the token is presented for payment.

Appendix U-1 
 
Appendix U.  Visa Digital Wallet 
A Visa Digital Wallet can be of two categories: 
• Pass-through Digital Wallet  
• Staged Digital Wallet 
Pass-through Digital Wallet: A digital wallet in which the payment device/method loaded into 
the wallet is actually used to conduct the overall transaction but the wallet form factor (e.g., 
mobile device) substitutes the original form factor (e.g., plastic card).  
A Pass-through Digital Wallet provides functionality to a cardholder that facilitates the following:  
• Allows usage at multiple merchants.  
• Stores a credential (account or token) supplied by the cardholder to the Digital Wallet 
Operator.  
• Completes a transaction by transferring the stored credential to the merchant without 
interrupting the flow of funds. 
A pass-through Digital Wallet Operator (DWO) must ensure the cardholder consents in writing 
to the use of his or her account in the wallet according to the new rules, and must not perform 
Visa payment services for another DWO. 
Staged Digital Wallet: A Staged Digital Wallet couples two transactions, Purchase and 
Funding, each of which individually relies on and retains the character of the original, underlying 
legacy transaction methods. This wallet provides functionality to a cardholder that facilitates the 
following: 
• Allows usage at multiple retailers.  
• Uses a Visa account number supplied by the cardholder to the Staged Digital Wallet 
Operator (SDWO). 
• Uses a separate account or accounts assigned by the SDWO to the cardholder.  
• Completes a transaction (via an SDWO) in more than one stage, in any order, as follows: 
 Purchase Transaction: Pays the retailer using the account assigned by the SDWO.  
 Funding Transaction: Uses the Visa account number provided by the cardholder to fund 
or reimburse the Staged Digital Wallet.

Appendix X-1 
 
Appendix X.  Online Refund/Refund Authorization 
Note: Please contact your First Data representative for availability of this functionality 
Today, cardholders have real-time, 24/7 access to their online banking apps through 
smartphones and other devices. They are more aware than ever of how quickly purchase 
information is updated to their account. However, cardholders also have become increasingly 
aware that the same flow of information does not exist on purchase returns. 
To align the purchase and return processes, an authorization was introduced on credit voucher 
(aka purchase return) transactions. This new credit voucher / purchase return authorization 
message will provide issuers with real-time information about returns, similar to that for 
purchases, which they must then provide to their cardholders.  
Merchants must send the Online Refund/Refund Authorization Indicator in Sub-table ID 11 of 
POS Additional Data Information (Table ID 32) in Appendix I (Variable Information Data 
Layouts) when participating in Online Refund/Refund Authorization program to get authorization 
for Merchandise Return transactions. Merchants who do not want Merchandise Return to be 
approved online must not send this field. 
The value of the Online Refund/Refund Authorization Indicator should be ‘Y’ for Visa, 
MasterCard, Amex, and Discover. 
When the Online Refund/Refund Authorization Indicator is included in a Merchandise Return 
transaction, this indicator should also be included in the subsequent reversal/follow-up 
transactions and Timeout reversals. 
Starting October, 2018, for certain merchants Visa will require a ‘real-time’ message using the 
Authorization system, prior to an existing Settlement System Refund. Impacted merchants have 
already been notified. All other merchants are expected to perform Visa online authorization 
effective April, 2020..  
A ‘real time’ message (like an Authorization) will advise the issuer and/or cardholder that a 
refund is pending. This will help to eliminate the delay between the merchant deciding to initiate 
a Refund and the visible impact on the cardholder’s account. 
It is expected that an Online Refund/Refund Authorization will only be declined if the Issuer 
cannot be reached or the cardholder account is not valid; however declining transactions for any 
reason is subject to the Issuer’s discretion. 
.

Appendix Y-1 
 
Appendix Y.  3-D Secure 
Introduction: “3-D Secure” is a general term for an advanced authentication solution 
implemented to reduce eCommerce fraud by verifying a cardholder’s identity in real time. Each 
of the major card brands has a 3-D Secure offering: Visa “Verified by Visa”, MasterCard 
“SecureCode”, American Express “Safekey”. This appendix provides detailed information on 
these services. 
 
How it Works: The 3-D Secure protocol operates in three domains: 
• Acquirer Domain – The Acquirer accepts eCommerce transaction data from the merchant 
and passes it to Visa/MasterCard/Amex/Discover (as applicable). 
• Issuer Domain – The Issuer is responsible for determining whether authentication is 
available for the card account presented in a purchase. 
• Interoperability Domain – Infrastructure created by the payment networks and software 
providers to enable the 3-D Secure protocol between the Acquirer Domain and the Issuer 
Domain 
 
The 3-D Secure process involves the following steps: 
1. The cardholder enters card information on the merchant’s site (that uses 3-D Secure) to 
purchase goods. 
2.  Merchant Plug-in (MPI) contacts the Directory Server (DS) to initiate an authentication 
request. 
3. The DS routes the authentication request to the appropriate Issuer Access Control 
Server (ACS). 
4. The DS sends the Issuer ACS response to the MPI. 
5. The cardholder is directed to the Issuer’s 3-D Secure browser page. The Issuer 
authenticates cardholder’s identity in a variety of ways, such as asking to enter password which 
the cardholder has previously set up with the Issuer, or requesting to enter an authentication 
code/OTP that has been sent to the cardholder’s registered email/mobile number  
6. The Issuer approves or declines the Authorization Request and returns the Authorization 
Response (containing cryptographic value along with ECI/Terminal Type (Position Nos. 9–10) 
values 25, 26, 27, 28 or 29 (as applicable) and other data) to the merchant. Refer to the below 
grid for the cryptographic values returned for each card brands: 
Card Brand Cryptographic Value 
Visa CAVV 
MasterCard AAV 
Amex AEVV 
7. The cardholder is redirected to the merchant’s site and the purchase is completed. 
 
Note: Contact your 3-D Secure representative for further details. 
 
VERIFIED BY VISA:

Appendix Y-2 
 
Verified by Visa (VbV) is an online service that verifies a cardholder’s ownership of an account, 
in real time, during an online payment transaction. It gives Visa card Issuers the ability to 
confirm a cardholder’s identity using a variety of authentication methods, including passwords, 
chip cards and digital certificates, providing merchants with real time authentication results 
during the checkout process. Verified by Visa is based on the 3-D Secure Protocol, which uses 
Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) encryption to collect and protect payment card information 
transmitted via the Internet. 
Merchants participating in Visa token service may (optionaly) support the TAVV in combination 
with 3-D Secure (3DS) CAVV for payment token-based transactions with 3-D Secure. 
Effective October 2018, Visa will support two separate cryptograms in the authorization 
message:  
1) The TAVV Cryptogram for payment token validation 
2) The 3DS CAVV cryptogram for cardholder authentication  
Note: Please contact your First Data representative for the availability of this functionality.

Note: The usages provided below are not exhaustive and all encompassing.

AMERICAN EXPRESS SAFEKEY  
American Express SafeKey (Amex SafeKey) is an online service that verifies a cardholder’s 
ownership of an account, in real time, during an online payment transaction. Amex SafeKey 
gives Amex card Issuers the ability to confirm a cardholder’s identity using a variety of 
authentication methods, including passwords, chip cards and digital certificates, providing 
merchants with real time authentication results during the checkout process. Amex SafeKey is 
based on the 3-D Secure Protocol, which uses Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) encryption to 
collect and protect payment card information transmitted via the Internet.  
SafeKey transactions coming from merchants will be sent with indicator “SK” followed by 56 
bytes of SafeKey data in base64 format. When the first 28 bytes of value is not applicable, it 
should be space filled.

Appendix Y-3 
 
Note: American Express Safekey is not available for OptBlue merchants. 
 
MASTERCARD SECURECODE 
MasterCard SecureCode is a solution designed to authenticate cardholders when paying online. 
SecureCode offers a mechanism for securing the Internet channel by strongly authenticating the 
cardholder at the point of interaction by providing a unique transaction-specific token that 
provides evidence that the cardholder originated the transaction. SecureCode uses 
MasterCard’s Universal Cardholder Authentication Field (UCAF) infrastructure to communicate 
the authentication information among the cardholder, Issuer, merchant and Acquirer.  
MasterCard SecureCode supports the 3-D Secure Protocol. MasterCard SecureCode requires 
merchants to install 3-D Secure v1.0.2 (or better) compliant Merchant Server Plug-In software. 
 
 
MASTERCARD DIGITAL SECURE REMOTE PAYMENT 
MasterCard has introduced a new data element for Digital Payment containing both cardholder 
authentication and token authentication in a more comprehensive manner to validate token 
transactions in electronic commerce environment. 
This feature enables merchants to take advantage of the security validation when both DSRP 
cryptogram and SecureCode/Identity Check AAVare present in same message. 
Merchants can support both Digital Secure Remote Payment (DSRP) cryptogram and 
SecureCode/Identity Check 3DS Accountholder Authentication Value (AAV) in the same request 
message. However, the UCAF Security level code (position ‘1 -2’) should be ‘21’ (Channel 
Encrypted). 
Merchants should use the UCAF data field for the MasterCard AAV cryptogram (Data segment 
111 table ID 36)  and should use the TAVV field (Segment 123) for all Token and DSRP 
cryptograms.

Appendix Z-1 
 
Appendix Z.  Stored Credential 
For definitions and use cases, refer to section 10.13.2.4.1 Stored Credentials. The use cases 
apply to Visa, MasterCard, Discover, and Amex.  
When storing credentials for the first time: 
• If no amount is due when credentials are stored for the first time, a $0.00 Account 
Verification transaction can be sent along with Value ‘I’ (Initial) in Data Element 111, 
Table ID 32 – POS Additional Data Information Sub table ID 08  
• If an amount is due when credentials are stored for cardholder-initiated stored credential 
transactions, Value ‘I’ (Initial) in Data Element 111, Table ID 32 – POS Additional Data 
Information Sub table ID 08   
• If an amount is due when credentials are stored for recurring or installment, the 
transaction must be identified as recurring (‘R’) or installment (‘I’)  
• The original POS Entry mode (for example: 02, 90 etc. respectively as defined in 
Appendix J) will be sent  
• For Unscheduled Merchant Initiated or Cardholder initiated Credential-on-File  
transactions, no recurring or installment indicators are required 
• Visa/Amex Transaction ID (Data Element 112, Table ID 28) and Discover Network 
Reference number (Data Element 112, Table ID 12) from response  should be stored 
and used for allsubsequent merchant-initiated COF transactions 
• Authorization amount should be stored for Discover transactions as it is later required for 
all subsequent merchant initiated Discover transactions 
• For MasterCard card type, Merchant needs to send MIT/CIT category and subcategory 
data with valid value as applicable to Merchant Initiated transaction (MIT) or Cardholder 
initiated transaction (CIT) for initial transaction while storing credential on file. Refer to 
Variable Information Indicator (Data Element 111), Table ID 56 (Stored Credentials 
Transaction Additional Data), Sub Table ID 09 for more details 
 
When initiating a recurring transaction using a stored credential MIT (Merchant Initiated 
Transaction) without active participation of the cardholder: 
• The transaction must be identified as ‘R’ (Recurring) 
• For all card types, Data Element 111, Table ID 32 – POS Additional Data Information, 
Sub table ID 08 should have value ‘C’ for Subsequent Credential on File 
 
• For all card types, POS Entry Mode value of ‘10’ must be submitted in Data Element 
111, Table ID 05 - Point-of-Service Entry Mode 
• For Merchant initiated COF transactions (MIT) where transactions are based on the 
stand-in instructions with cardholder, Merchants should use the appropriate recurring 
indicators and store the original transaction identifier to be used in the subsequent 
transactions. 
• Include the Merchant Initiated (MIT) indicator using Data Element 111, Table ID 49, Sub 
Table ID 02, Value ‘M’. 
• CVV2 Data must not be sent 
• Visa/Amex Transaction ID (Data Element 111, Table ID 44) and Discover Network 
Reference Number (Data Element 111, Table ID 15) should be included in this 
subsequent request

Appendix AA-1 
 
Appendix AA. TransArmor Processing Considerations 
 
TransArmor is a processing option provided by FirstData that provides more secure transaction 
processing using encryption and tokenization.  
 
When initializing a terminal for TransArmor Processing, a TransArmor Key Load should be 
performed to obtain the Key ID and Key to be used for encryption purposes. In addition, a 
RegiStart transaction should be performed to register the device with TransArmor. These 
functions are described in the ATL105 Specifications Update for TransArmor Processing 
document. 
 
The available encryption types for TransArmor processing are: 
• RSA encryption 
• TA-VE Cipher Hidden Encryption 
• TDES/DUKPT 
• Ingenico On Guard FPE 
• AES DUKPT 
 
The following are specific considerations required in transaction processing in order to use 
TransArmor. 
Data Element 2 – Account Number 
For TransArmor processing, the Account Number field is replaced by the TAP header and 
EDATA. The general format for this data is: 
TAPnnnnnnxyyyyyyyyyyyzzzz[EDATA] 
Where, 
 TAP = 3-byte TransArmor Indicator 
 nnnnnn = 6-byte Sequence Number of the transaction that matches the value 
in Element No. 86 (Sequence Number) 
 x = 1-byte [EDATA] Identifier that describes the content of [EDATA] 
 yyyyyyyyyyy = 11-byte Key ID 
 zzzz = 4-byte Token Type ID. 
 Valid Values: XXXX = Single use or MultiPay Token; 4-byte 
  alphanumeric value assigned by First Data 
 [EDATA] = contents are dependent on the information in the TAP header and 
whether the transaction is an initial transaction or a subsequent. 
Maximum length of encrypted data is 400 bytes. 
Note: On all subsequent transactions, the unencrypted expiration date should be sent in Data 
Element 12, Card Discretionary Block Data, as it would for non-TransArmor transactions. 
Note: In all cases, the TransArmor token to be used in the subsequent transaction is contained 
in the Account Number field in the initial transaction response. 
Note: In the case of the Initial Transaction Request for the PKI Encryption and Tokenization 
method, 2 zeros followed by the first 6 bytes of the Merchant Number assigned by BUYPASS

Data Element 12 – Card Discretionary Data 
For TransArmor processing, the expiration date must be stored for subsequent transactions 
associated with a token. 
Data Element 26 – Decline Code 
For a TransArmor Token Only transaction that has been declined because BUYPASS cannot 
retrieve the necessary token for the associated PAN, the decline code 4M will be returned to the 
POS. 
Data Element 30 – Download Indicator 
A value of 8 in this field indicates that the terminal needs to update its Key ID and Key because 
the current Key ID is due to expire or has expired. 
Data Element 48 – Load Type 
A value of K in this field indicates that the load being requested is a TransArmor Key and Key ID 
request. 
Data Element 83 – Response Code 
The following values are specific to TransArmor Key Load processing: 
K Approved—TransArmor Load 
L Rejected for one of the following reasons— 
1) Merchant is not TransArmor enabled 
2) Signing Key is invalid or outdated 
Data Element 102 – Terminal Identifier 
For TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization Load Request, the Device Type should be 
“++” regardless of the actual device type of the terminal. 
Segment 111, Table ID 52 – Additional TransArmor Data 
In some TransArmor implementations, a longer Key ID and/or a Special device type can be 
specified using this Data Element.

Appendix AB-1 
 
Appendix AB. Purchase Repayment 
 
Purchase repayments are type of installment payments submitted by third party installment 
provider or payment facilitators. Third party installment providers referred here are the 
merchants that are different from the retailer selling goods or services. 
Use case for Purchase repayments includes post purchase payments, Buy now Pay later 
services provided by third party service provider.

Appendix AD-1 
 
Appendix AD. Real Time Account Updater 
 
Definition: 
The Real Time Account Updater enables the secure electronic exchange of account information 
updates between participating issuers and acquirers for merchants who securely store the 
Cardholder account information for future recurring / subsequent transactions (for example, 
credentials on file). 
 
Transaction processing rules: 
The transaction must be from a participating acquirer and must be a card not present 
transaction as identified by any of the following criteria:  
• Credential on file transaction  
• Instalment payment  
• Recurring payment 
The merchant must register and certify with First Data to participate in the Real Time Account 
Updater process. 
Note: For further details and requirements, please contact your Account Representative.  
Participating merchant should send the Account Updater Request Indicator field (Variable 
Information segment 111, Table ID 060, Sub table ID 01) as trigger in request messages for all 
Instalment, Recurring, and Credential on File transactions. First Data will determine whether the 
transaction qualifies for Real Time Account Updater before requesting account information 
update from the association. 
Note: Merchants using Real Time Account Updater should refer to Account Number - Data 
Element 2 and Card Discretionary Block Data - Data Element 12 for additional information.

Appendix AE-1 
 
Appendix AE. Visa Estimated and Incremental 
Authorization Transactions 
 
* MCC 4121, 5411 - Estimated and Incremental authorizations are allowed for Card Not Present 
transactions only. 
* MCC 5552 – Estimated and Incremental authorizations for EV transactions. 
For permitted merchants, an estimated or initial authorization must be included in an estimated 
or initial authorization request, and must be used when the final amount is unknown. In addition, 
merchants and acquirers must ensure that each incremental authorization requests: 
• Only follows an estimated / initial authorization. 
• Contains an incremental authorization indicator - BUYPASS Host identifies the 
incremental authorization transaction by the approval code returned (Authorization 
Identification Response). Once identified as incremental authorization transaction, the 
Host will send out the incremental indicator on behalf of the merchant to Visa. 
• Contains the same Sequence Number as the estimated or initial transaction request. 
• Contains the same Transaction Identifier in Segment  as the estimated or initial 
transaction request. 
• Contains the same Terminal transaction number (Table ID 63 in Segment 111) as the 
estimated or initial transaction request.  
 
Example: Customer A checks in a hotel for 3 days. The merchant uses Customer A’s credit or 
signature debit card (common AID - routed to Visa if processed as dual message) and sends 
the estimated auth indicator as ‘1’ in the Acquirer Trace Data – Sub Table ID 09 in the initial 
authorization request. At the end of Day 3, Customer A extends his stay at the same hotel and 
also avails a few other services, such as laundry service. The subsequent transactions must not 
carry the estimated authorization indicator in Sub Table ID 09. BUYPASS Host will identify the 
transactions as incremental based on the approval code that the merchant sends in 
Authorization Identification Response in the subsequent transactions. Merchants must send the 
final amount in the completion transaction message. 
For cruise lines, lodging merchants, and Car/ Vehicle Rental merchants, an approval response 
to the estimated authorization and any subsequent incremental authorization will expire 14 days 
after the initial estimated authorization. For other rental merchants, such as trailer parks and 
campgrounds, an approval response to the estimated authorization and any subsequent 
incremental authorization will expire seven days after the initial estimated authorization. 
Merchants with stays or rentals that exceed this period will be subject to chargebacks for no 
authorizations unless they complete the first transaction and then initiate the second transaction 
on or before day 14 or day seven, as applicable by MCCs.
